## 2023 Honda CR-V Review

[![Image 8: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   The Honda CR-V is our Compact SUV Best Buy of 2023
*   Superb in so many areas

### Cons

*   Slight (if warranted) price premiums

### What's New?

*   Totally redesigned for 2023

[![Image 9: 2023 Best Buy Awards badge](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/best-buy-logo-badge-2023-275w.png)](https://www.kbb.com/awards/best-buy-awards-2023-honda-cr-v-compact-suv)

Here we are, welcoming generation six of the perennially popular Honda CR-V compact SUV into the world. Expertise gained and lessons learned from the previous generations combine with fresh technology and manufacturing techniques to create the best-ever CR-V.

It wasn’t even as if the 2022 version was out-classed by the competition. It was still highly recommendable for its space, safety, reliability, economy, and resale values. The CR-V deserves its fine reputation for being good in a multitude of ways.

This is like when a world-record-holding athlete posts a faster time or lifts a heavier weight. Honda knows that when you’re standing still, you’re really going backward. Because everyone else is on that same path of improvement. For now, though, the 2023 CR-V has strengthened its position as the cream of the compact SUV crop.

The similarly all-new 2023 [CR-V Hybrid](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v-hybrid) is reviewed separately.

### 2023 Honda CR-V Pricing

2023 Honda CR-V pricing starts at $25,700 for the CR-V LX Sport Utility 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $31,205 when new. The range-topping 2023 CR-V EX-L Sport Utility 4D starts at $28,300 today, originally priced from $37,055.

The Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price for any individual used vehicle can vary greatly according to mileage, condition, location, and other factors. The prices here reflect what buyers are currently paying for used 2023 Honda CR-V models in typical condition when purchasing from a dealership. These prices are updated weekly.

### Driving the Honda CR-V

Here’s a little snippet from our notebook after driving the 2023 CR-V: “Beautifully tuned suspension, comfortable yet precise.” To be honest, earlier incarnations of the CR-V have been a bit of a yawn to drive. This one is different.

It responds quickly and sweetly to inputs like steering and braking, so the driver feels completely in control — as well as being kept aware of what’s going on with great outward vision, enhanced by things like standard-issue blind-spot monitoring.

The CR-V will still appeal to everyone who just wants a stable, comfy and reliable compact SUV for everyday driving. It’s just that it can be more enjoyable now.

In these days of push-button and rotating gear selectors, it’s almost odd to see a conventional shift lever in the new CR-V. But we know many buyers will welcome the familiarity.

_We’ve spent hundreds of hours driving and researching the current collection of [compact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/suv/best-compact-suvs/), including this new Honda CR-V._

### Smart, Spacious Interior

Stretching the wheelbase by a couple of inches (the distance between the front and rear axles) has increased rear legroom and brings a benefit to ride quality. Not that CR-V owners in the past have ever been deprived in these areas. It does, however, show how Honda has brought incremental improvements to the 2023 CR-V that all combine to make a tangible difference.

Up front are what Honda calls Body Stabilizing Seats, designed to promote ideal posture and reduce fatigue. They certainly feel comfortable, supportive, and fine for long driving stints. The rear seats gain seat belt reminders and their occupants now enjoy a generous 41 inches of legroom.

![Image 10: A look at the interior of the 2023 Honda CR-V](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/2023-honda-cr-v-interior.jpg)

We like the crisp yet pleasant-looking graphics in the driver information display between the two round gauges, as well as the overall quality of materials. The L of EX-L signifies leather seating surfaces, by the way. Meanwhile, the mesh strip running across the dashboard is novel.

With rivals fitting 12-inch infotainment touchscreens, the 9-inch display in the [highest EX-L trim](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/heres-what-you-get-on-a-fully-loaded-2023-honda-cr-v/) level seems a little on the small side. And the EX has an even smaller, 7-inch touchscreen. At least there’s a physical volume control.

Cargo space receives a boost. Behind the rear seats there’s a massive 39.3 cubic feet — visibly more than, say, the Kia Sportage. The level of the cargo floor is also conveniently low. With the rear seats folded down, maximum volume is 76.5 cubic feet, as good as this compact SUV class gets.

### Confident Exterior

We think there’s a maturity to the new CR-V’s exterior design. As there should be, considering this is the sixth generation. But where previous models tried to be the most anonymous thing in the parking lot, there’s now greater presence — in a tasteful way.

Compared with the outgoing CR-V, this new model is longer by just over a couple of inches, and ever-so-slightly wider. Some of the subtler touches include a wider and more upright windshield, contributing to excellent outward vision. Running boards, fender flares, and a liftgate spoiler are all optional.

### Our Favorite Features and Tech

**Apple CarPlay/Android Auto**  
 Smartphone integration has become pretty much a necessity, using apps for things like navigation and spoken-word text replies. It’s standard in the 2023 CR-V and the higher EX-L trim also enables wireless connectivity for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

**Wireless charging**  
 Another EX-L feature. Just place a capable smartphone on the charging pad in the center console and it all happens automatically.

**All-wheel drive**  
 For buyers living in areas where the weather gets rough, it’s no doubt worth the extra money for the added reassurance of all-wheel drive. It’s optional with both 2023 CR-V trims.

**Hill descent control**  
 This is new for a CR-V and it’s not just a feature accompanying the all-wheel-drive system; it comes as standard with front-drive versions as well. The driver sets a slow speed (between 2 mph and 12 mph) to negotiate a treacherous downward slope. The CR-V handles the throttle, transmission, and brakes. With feet off the pedals, the driver just steers.

**8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat**  
 OK, this might seem a bit mundane, but the base trim levels of most compact SUVs have manual adjustment. It’s higher-spec features like this that help justify the CR-V’s pricing. The EX-L adds memory settings, great for when there’s more than one regular driver.

**Traffic Jam Assist**  
 As if to underline the pricing argument just above, this is also standard in the [popular EX trim](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/this-is-the-most-popular-2023-honda-cr-v/). It works with the lane-keeping system, adding slight steering corrections at speeds below 45 mph right down to a complete stop. Anything that helps relieve the tedium of city traffic is a plus.

![Image 11: A red 2023 Honda CR-V stationary and pictured from the rear.](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/2023-honda-cr-v-exterior-rear-red.jpg)

### Engine & Transmission

Turbocharging has evolved to such sophisticated heights that it can perform the neat trick of maximizing power output while still achieving decent fuel economy.

The 2023 CR-V’s turbocharged 1.5-liter 4-cylinder engine itself is another example of evolution rather than being completely new. It has the same muscle as before — 190 horsepower and 179 lb-ft of torque — and returns identical fuel economy figures. But that’s fine. We had no complaints about its predecessor, except for the puny 1,500-pound tow rating — which hasn’t changed with this new generation. Not many people use a compact SUV for towing, though.

An automatic transmission sends drive to the front wheels (FWD) in standard form. All-wheel drive (AWD) is optional.

**1.5-liter turbocharged 4-cylinder engine**  
 190 horsepower @ 6,000 rpm  
 179 lb-ft of torque @ 1,700-5,000 rpm  
 EPA city/highway fuel economy: 28/34 mpg (FWD), 27/32 mpg (AWD)

More CR-V fuel economy information is available on the [EPA’s website](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/PowerSearch.do?action=noform&path=1&year1=2023&year2=2023&make=Honda&baseModel=CR-V&srchtyp=ymm&pageno=1&rowLimit=50).

### **Outstanding Safety Ratings**

The 2023 Honda CR-V is an [IIHS Top Safety Pick+](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/vehicle/honda/cr-v-4-door-suv/2023), which is the highest honor available from the safety watchdog group. It earns this honor with a long list of standard safety features like automatic emergency braking, lane-keep assist, blind-spot monitoring, and more.

### **3-Year/36,000-Mile Warranty**

The basic new-vehicle warranty for the 2023 CR-V compact SUV is three years or 36,000 miles, whichever happens first. The powertrain’s warranty lasts for five years or 60,000 miles. Honda also adds complimentary maintenance for the first two years or 24,000 miles.

## 2023 Honda CR-V Safety

### Safety Features & Technology

### **Forward collision warning**

The standard set of driver aids in every new CR-V compact SUV is called Honda Sensing. It includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, plus road departure mitigation, lane-departure warning, and adaptive cruise control with a low-speed follow function.

### **Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert**

This is another component of the standard Honda Sensing array, warning drivers of vehicles in adjacent lanes as well as anything approaching while reversing the CR-V out of a parking space.

### **Low Speed Braking Control**

One of the extra features in the EX-L trim, this includes front and rear parking sensors. If the CR-V is being maneuvered too close to a potential hazard, there are audible and visual warnings, then an automatic emergency stop if necessary, holding the brakes for a few seconds. It operates between 2 mph and 4 mph.

## FAQs

#### How much is a 2023 Honda CR-V?

The manufacturer’s suggested retail price on a new 2023 Honda CR-V EX with front-wheel drive is $28,410. The better-equipped EX-L starts at $34,260.

#### Is the 2023 Honda CR-V a good SUV?

The CR-V compact SUV has always been good at getting many things right, adding up to an unbeatable package. This all-new generation attains the highest level to date.

#### Does the 2023 Honda CR-V have all-wheel drive?

Yes, all-wheel drive is available on both the EX and EX-L trims of the 2023 CR-V compact SUV.

#### Is the 2023 Honda CR-V a good vehicle?

Yes, the 2023 Honda CR-V is a good car, as reflected by its above-average Kelley Blue Book rating of 4.8 out of 5.

#### What is the MPG for a 2023 Honda CR-V?

The 2023 Honda CR-V is rated to return city/highway fuel economy of 27/32 mpg.

#### How much should a 2023 Honda CR-V cost?

Used 2023 Honda CR-V prices currently range from $25,700 for the LX Sport Utility 4D to $28,300 for the EX-L Sport Utility 4D when purchasing from a dealership, depending on a range of factors like equipment, mileage, and condition.

#### What's the cheapest Honda CR-V?

The cheapest 2023 Honda CR-V is the LX Sport Utility 4D, with a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $25,700.

#### Is the 2023 Honda CR-V reliable?

The 2023 Honda CR-V is part of the 6th-generation CR-V, which our owners give an above-average reliability rating of 4.6 out of 5.

## 2023 Honda CR-V Review

[![Image 8: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   The Honda CR-V is our Compact SUV Best Buy of 2023
*   Superb in so many areas

### Cons

*   Slight (if warranted) price premiums

### What's New?

*   Totally redesigned for 2023

[![Image 9: 2023 Best Buy Awards badge](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/best-buy-logo-badge-2023-275w.png)](https://www.kbb.com/awards/best-buy-awards-2023-honda-cr-v-compact-suv)

Here we are, welcoming generation six of the perennially popular Honda CR-V compact SUV into the world. Expertise gained and lessons learned from the previous generations combine with fresh technology and manufacturing techniques to create the best-ever CR-V.

It wasn’t even as if the 2022 version was out-classed by the competition. It was still highly recommendable for its space, safety, reliability, economy, and resale values. The CR-V deserves its fine reputation for being good in a multitude of ways.

This is like when a world-record-holding athlete posts a faster time or lifts a heavier weight. Honda knows that when you’re standing still, you’re really going backward. Because everyone else is on that same path of improvement. For now, though, the 2023 CR-V has strengthened its position as the cream of the compact SUV crop.

The similarly all-new 2023 [CR-V Hybrid](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v-hybrid) is reviewed separately.

### 2023 Honda CR-V Pricing

2023 Honda CR-V pricing starts at $25,700 for the CR-V LX Sport Utility 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $31,205 when new. The range-topping 2023 CR-V EX-L Sport Utility 4D starts at $28,300 today, originally priced from $37,055.

|  |  | Original MSRP | KBB Fair Purchase Price (national avg.) |  |
| --- | --- |
|  | [LX Sport Utility 4D](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v/2023/lx-sport-utility-4d/) | $31,205 | $25,700 |  |
|  | [EX Sport Utility 4D](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v/2023/ex-sport-utility-4d/) | $34,405 | $26,300 |  |
|  | [EX-L Sport Utility 4D](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v/2023/ex-l-sport-utility-4d/) | $37,055 | $28,300 |  |

The Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price for any individual used vehicle can vary greatly according to mileage, condition, location, and other factors. The prices here reflect what buyers are currently paying for used 2023 Honda CR-V models in typical condition when purchasing from a dealership. These prices are updated weekly.

### Driving the Honda CR-V

Here’s a little snippet from our notebook after driving the 2023 CR-V: “Beautifully tuned suspension, comfortable yet precise.” To be honest, earlier incarnations of the CR-V have been a bit of a yawn to drive. This one is different.

It responds quickly and sweetly to inputs like steering and braking, so the driver feels completely in control — as well as being kept aware of what’s going on with great outward vision, enhanced by things like standard-issue blind-spot monitoring.

The CR-V will still appeal to everyone who just wants a stable, comfy and reliable compact SUV for everyday driving. It’s just that it can be more enjoyable now.

In these days of push-button and rotating gear selectors, it’s almost odd to see a conventional shift lever in the new CR-V. But we know many buyers will welcome the familiarity.

_We’ve spent hundreds of hours driving and researching the current collection of [compact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/suv/best-compact-suvs/), including this new Honda CR-V._

### Smart, Spacious Interior

Stretching the wheelbase by a couple of inches (the distance between the front and rear axles) has increased rear legroom and brings a benefit to ride quality. Not that CR-V owners in the past have ever been deprived in these areas. It does, however, show how Honda has brought incremental improvements to the 2023 CR-V that all combine to make a tangible difference.

Up front are what Honda calls Body Stabilizing Seats, designed to promote ideal posture and reduce fatigue. They certainly feel comfortable, supportive, and fine for long driving stints. The rear seats gain seat belt reminders and their occupants now enjoy a generous 41 inches of legroom.

![Image 10: A look at the interior of the 2023 Honda CR-V](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/2023-honda-cr-v-interior.jpg)

We like the crisp yet pleasant-looking graphics in the driver information display between the two round gauges, as well as the overall quality of materials. The L of EX-L signifies leather seating surfaces, by the way. Meanwhile, the mesh strip running across the dashboard is novel.

With rivals fitting 12-inch infotainment touchscreens, the 9-inch display in the [highest EX-L trim](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/heres-what-you-get-on-a-fully-loaded-2023-honda-cr-v/) level seems a little on the small side. And the EX has an even smaller, 7-inch touchscreen. At least there’s a physical volume control.

Cargo space receives a boost. Behind the rear seats there’s a massive 39.3 cubic feet — visibly more than, say, the Kia Sportage. The level of the cargo floor is also conveniently low. With the rear seats folded down, maximum volume is 76.5 cubic feet, as good as this compact SUV class gets.

### Confident Exterior

We think there’s a maturity to the new CR-V’s exterior design. As there should be, considering this is the sixth generation. But where previous models tried to be the most anonymous thing in the parking lot, there’s now greater presence — in a tasteful way.

Compared with the outgoing CR-V, this new model is longer by just over a couple of inches, and ever-so-slightly wider. Some of the subtler touches include a wider and more upright windshield, contributing to excellent outward vision. Running boards, fender flares, and a liftgate spoiler are all optional.

### Our Favorite Features and Tech

**Apple CarPlay/Android Auto**  
 Smartphone integration has become pretty much a necessity, using apps for things like navigation and spoken-word text replies. It’s standard in the 2023 CR-V and the higher EX-L trim also enables wireless connectivity for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

**Wireless charging**  
 Another EX-L feature. Just place a capable smartphone on the charging pad in the center console and it all happens automatically.

**All-wheel drive**  
 For buyers living in areas where the weather gets rough, it’s no doubt worth the extra money for the added reassurance of all-wheel drive. It’s optional with both 2023 CR-V trims.

**Hill descent control**  
 This is new for a CR-V and it’s not just a feature accompanying the all-wheel-drive system; it comes as standard with front-drive versions as well. The driver sets a slow speed (between 2 mph and 12 mph) to negotiate a treacherous downward slope. The CR-V handles the throttle, transmission, and brakes. With feet off the pedals, the driver just steers.

**8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat**  
 OK, this might seem a bit mundane, but the base trim levels of most compact SUVs have manual adjustment. It’s higher-spec features like this that help justify the CR-V’s pricing. The EX-L adds memory settings, great for when there’s more than one regular driver.

**Traffic Jam Assist**  
 As if to underline the pricing argument just above, this is also standard in the [popular EX trim](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/this-is-the-most-popular-2023-honda-cr-v/). It works with the lane-keeping system, adding slight steering corrections at speeds below 45 mph right down to a complete stop. Anything that helps relieve the tedium of city traffic is a plus.

![Image 11: A red 2023 Honda CR-V stationary and pictured from the rear.](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/2023-honda-cr-v-exterior-rear-red.jpg)

### Engine & Transmission

Turbocharging has evolved to such sophisticated heights that it can perform the neat trick of maximizing power output while still achieving decent fuel economy.

The 2023 CR-V’s turbocharged 1.5-liter 4-cylinder engine itself is another example of evolution rather than being completely new. It has the same muscle as before — 190 horsepower and 179 lb-ft of torque — and returns identical fuel economy figures. But that’s fine. We had no complaints about its predecessor, except for the puny 1,500-pound tow rating — which hasn’t changed with this new generation. Not many people use a compact SUV for towing, though.

An automatic transmission sends drive to the front wheels (FWD) in standard form. All-wheel drive (AWD) is optional.

**1.5-liter turbocharged 4-cylinder engine**  
 190 horsepower @ 6,000 rpm  
 179 lb-ft of torque @ 1,700-5,000 rpm  
 EPA city/highway fuel economy: 28/34 mpg (FWD), 27/32 mpg (AWD)

More CR-V fuel economy information is available on the [EPA’s website](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/PowerSearch.do?action=noform&path=1&year1=2023&year2=2023&make=Honda&baseModel=CR-V&srchtyp=ymm&pageno=1&rowLimit=50).

### **Outstanding Safety Ratings**

The 2023 Honda CR-V is an [IIHS Top Safety Pick+](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/vehicle/honda/cr-v-4-door-suv/2023), which is the highest honor available from the safety watchdog group. It earns this honor with a long list of standard safety features like automatic emergency braking, lane-keep assist, blind-spot monitoring, and more.

### **3-Year/36,000-Mile Warranty**

The basic new-vehicle warranty for the 2023 CR-V compact SUV is three years or 36,000 miles, whichever happens first. The powertrain’s warranty lasts for five years or 60,000 miles. Honda also adds complimentary maintenance for the first two years or 24,000 miles.

## 2023 Honda CR-V Safety

### Safety Features & Technology

### **Forward collision warning**

The standard set of driver aids in every new CR-V compact SUV is called Honda Sensing. It includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, plus road departure mitigation, lane-departure warning, and adaptive cruise control with a low-speed follow function.

### **Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert**

This is another component of the standard Honda Sensing array, warning drivers of vehicles in adjacent lanes as well as anything approaching while reversing the CR-V out of a parking space.

One of the extra features in the EX-L trim, this includes front and rear parking sensors. If the CR-V is being maneuvered too close to a potential hazard, there are audible and visual warnings, then an automatic emergency stop if necessary, holding the brakes for a few seconds. It operates between 2 mph and 4 mph.

## Is the Honda CR-V a 7-Seater? – 2023 Honda CR-V Dimensions

So, is the Honda CR-V a seven-seater? While the 2023 Honda CR-V seats are designed for maximum comfort, it is technically only meant for five passengers. Although, if you’re looking for a Honda SUV that’s just as comfortable as the Honda CR-V but offers three rows of seating, you’ll want to explore the [new Honda Pilot](https://www.hondaofdanbury.com/new-vehicles/pilot/).

With that being said, that doesn’t mean that the Honda CR-V dimensions are cramped. In fact, you’ll find that there’s plenty of room for everyone to spread out on Bridgewater, CT, adventures in the new Honda CR-V:

*   **Front/Rear Headroom:** 38.2 inches/38.2 inches
*   **Front/Rear Shoulder Room:** 57.9 inches/55.9 inches
*   **Front/Rear Hip Room:** 55.6 inches/52.6 inches
*   **Fron/Rear Legroom:** 41.3 inches/41.0 inches
*   **Passenger Volume:** 103.5 cubic feet

## What’s the 2023 Honda CR-V Cargo Space Like?

It’s easy to get comfortable no matter where you’re sitting in the 2023 Honda CR-V but you’ll find that if no one’s riding along with you when you’re running errands around Poughkeepsie, NY, you’ll get tons of cargo space to accommodate a wide variety of items. Here are the 2023 Honda CR-V cargo space dimensions:

*   **Cargo Volume With Rear Seats Up:** 39.3 cubic feet
*   **Cargo Volume With Rear Seats Down:**76.5 cubic feet

## Is the Honda CR-V a 7-Seater? – 2023 Honda CR-V Dimensions

So, is the Honda CR-V a seven-seater? While the 2023 Honda CR-V seats are designed for maximum comfort, it is technically only meant for five passengers. Although, if you’re looking for a Honda SUV that’s just as comfortable as the Honda CR-V but offers three rows of seating, you’ll want to explore the [new Honda Pilot](https://www.hondaofdanbury.com/new-vehicles/pilot/).

With that being said, that doesn’t mean that the Honda CR-V dimensions are cramped. In fact, you’ll find that there’s plenty of room for everyone to spread out on Bridgewater, CT, adventures in the new Honda CR-V:

*   **Front/Rear Headroom:** 38.2 inches/38.2 inches
*   **Front/Rear Shoulder Room:** 57.9 inches/55.9 inches
*   **Front/Rear Hip Room:** 55.6 inches/52.6 inches
*   **Fron/Rear Legroom:** 41.3 inches/41.0 inches
*   **Passenger Volume:** 103.5 cubic feet

## What’s the 2023 Honda CR-V Cargo Space Like?

It’s easy to get comfortable no matter where you’re sitting in the 2023 Honda CR-V but you’ll find that if no one’s riding along with you when you’re running errands around Poughkeepsie, NY, you’ll get tons of cargo space to accommodate a wide variety of items. Here are the 2023 Honda CR-V cargo space dimensions:

*   **Cargo Volume With Rear Seats Up:** 39.3 cubic feet
*   **Cargo Volume With Rear Seats Down:**76.5 cubic feet

## 2023 Honda CR-V Interior Highlights

The latest Honda CR-V model is equipped with innovative technology and a wide range of amenities to keep you comfortable when you’re out on the road. Take a look at some interior highlights of the 2023 Honda CR-V below:

*   Dual-zone automatic climate control
*   Heated steering wheel
*   9.0-inch touchscreen
*   Wireless Apple CarPlay®/Android Auto™

The Honda CR-V interior seats up to five Pittsford passengers, accommodates up to 75.8 cubic feet of cargo space, and provides a wide range of comfort, convenience, and entertainment features. Keep reading to learn more about CR-V seating, CR-V cargo space, and so much more!

## 2022 Honda CR-V Seating

The 2022 Honda CR-V seating capacity is five, so you can bring along your closest friends for your Webster adventures. What’s more, the CR-V’s seating is customizable, thanks to a 60/40 split rear seatback, so you can adjust your passenger space and cargo space as necessary. Second-row passengers will also appreciate available amenities such as:

*   Rear seat climate control
*   A rear center armrest with cupholders
*   Rear-seat heater ducts
*   Rear-window defroster

Front passengers can also enjoy available comforts that include:

*   Automatic climate control
*   Heated front seats
*   Front driver’s seat with 12-way power adjustment and 4-way lumbar support
*   Front passenger’s seat with 4-way power adjustment
*   Power door and tailgate locks
*   Power windows with auto-up/down driver’s and front passenger’s window
*   Driver-side garment hook
*   Driver’s and front passenger’s vanity mirror

## 2022 Honda CR-V Cabin Dimensions

When you step inside of the Honda CR-V cabin, you’ll be thoroughly pleased with the sheer amount of space that it provides. Here’s a breakdown of the CR-V cargo space dimensions and CR-V passenger space dimensions:

*   Up to 105.9 cubic feet of passenger volume (Honda CR-V LX, Special Edition trim)
*   Up to 102.9 cubic feet of passenger volume (Honda CR-V EX, EX-L, Touring trims)
*   Up to 39.2 cubic feet / 75.8 cubic feet* of cargo space (rear seats up/down for the Honda CR-V LX, Special Edition trim)
*   Up to 39.2 cubic feet / 75.8 cubic feet* (Gas); 33.2 cubic feet / 68.7 cubic feet* (Hybrid) (rear seats up/down for the Honda CR-V EX, EX-L, Touring trims)

Now that you have an overview of the 2022 Honda CR-V interior dimensions, you may be curious about its dimensions on an individual, seating level. You nor your passengers have to worry about being cramped and uncomfortable when inside the CR-V cabin:

*   **Headroom (front/rear)**: 40.1/39.2 inches
*   **Legroom (front/rear)**: 41.3/40.4 inches
*   **Shoulder Room (front/rear)**: 57.9/55.6 inches
*   **Hiproom (front/rear)**: 55.1/49.5 inches

## FAQs

### Is the Honda CR-V a 4 or 6 cylinder?

All trim levels of the 2023 CR-V feature a 4 cylinder engine.

### Does the 2023 Honda CR-V have a turbo?

Yes, the following 2023 CR-V trims have turbo engines: LX Sport Utility 4D with a 4-Cyl, Turbo, 1.5 Liter, EX Sport Utility 4D with a 4-Cyl, Turbo, 1.5 Liter, etc.

### What features does a 2023 CR-V have?

2023 Honda CR-V features include AM/FM Radio, Bluetooth Wireless Technology, and Child Door Locks.

### How much horsepower does a 2023 CR-V have?

All 2023 CR-V trim variations have 190 horsepower.

### Is the Honda CR-V underpowered?

It depends on your definition of underpowered. All 2023 CR-V trim variations have 190 horsepower.

### Is the Honda CR-V fuel efficient?

All trim levels of the 2023 CR-V get 29 MPG, with 27 MPG in the city and 32 MPG on the highway.

# Video: Testing The 2023 Honda CR-V Hybrid

By![Image 3](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/sean-tucker.jpg?w=400&quality=75&strip=all)[Sean Tucker](https://www.kbb.com/author/seantucker/ "Posts By Sean Tucker")10/19/2022 7:38am

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QiPT4s_HSH8)

[Honda has an all-new CR-V for 2023](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/honda-reveals-all-new-2023-cr-v/), available with a 190-horsepower turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and the solid value you expect of the CR-V name. But there’s also a more powerful, 204-horsepower version. It’s the most fuel-efficient model, the [2023 CR-V Hybrid](https://www.kbb.com/honda/cr-v-hybrid/).

“The Honda CR-V has been on the road for more than 20 years, and you see them everywhere,” says our Mike Danger. “But there’s good reason for that.”

Mike recently got the chance to test drive the new CR-V hybrid on California roads.

His verdict? It’s pretty much the solid base hit you expect, though it has a “more rugged and handsome look” than the last generation. “If you’re looking for fuel efficiency, good tech, and a nice, roomy interior, this may be a good option for you.”

See how the CR-V fits Mike’s 6-foot-4-inch frame, and watch him experiment with its enhanced engine sounds and show you how to have fun in one of the most predictable vehicles on the market in the video.

# 2023 Honda CR-V Specs

![Image 9: 2023 Honda CR-V](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964334)  
 The [Honda CR-V](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/) has been one of the most popular vehicles in its class for quite a while now, offering drivers sporty performance, a comfortable and versatile cabin space, and a wide array of convenient features. But Honda is always innovating, and with the redesigned next-generation 2023 CR-V, Bayonne-area drivers can expect even more from this well-rounded and fun-to-drive SUV. Learn all about the 2023 Honda CR-V specs, price, and features in this guide from Metro Honda, then check out our [new Honda inventory](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/) in Jersey City today, as well as the recent redesign, fuel economy, and towing capacity!

[New CR-V Inventory](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/)[Continue Your Honda Research](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/manufacturer-information/)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Redesign

Here are some of the highlights of the 2023 Honda CR-V specs:

### Exterior Styling

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V has been redesigned to offer a bold profile that is both rugged and refined with a **large black mesh grille** that is reminiscent of the [Honda Ridgeline](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/). The Sport and Sport Touring hybrid models receive an even more striking refresh of the front and rear fascia, befitting their sporty performance capabilities.

### Larger, Inside and Out

*       *   One thing Newark-area drivers are sure to notice is that the 2023 Honda CR-V is bigger than the previous edition. In fact, the 2023 CR-V is **2.7 inches long and close to a half inch wider**. In addition, the 1.6 inches added to the wheelbase has resulted in more interior space, especially for rear seat passengers.

### Revised Body Structure

*       *   Along with the styling upgrades, the 2023 Honda CR-V has been built to be **15% stiffer torsionally**, which boosts performance, efficiency, and safety.

### Interior Features

*       *   The modern interior design of the 2023 Honda CR-V features a **honeycomb dash insert** similar to that offered in the new [2023 HR-V](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/2023-hr-v/). As we mentioned previously, the larger proportions of the 2023 CR-V increase the interior space, with the rear legroom expanding by about half an inch. A **standard 7-inch touchscreen** includes [Android Auto™ and Apple CarPlay®](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/connect-to-apple-carplay-android-auto/) capability, while upper trims come with a 9-inch display with wireless smartphone integration. You will also be able to look forward to the advanced driver-assist systems offered with the standard [Honda Sensing®](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/what-is-honda-sensing/).

### Performance

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V specs include t**wo available powertrains: a standard internal combustion engine and a hybrid system**. The gas-powered model will be equipped with a turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and a revised continuously variable transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive is standard on the entry-level model, with [Real Time All-Wheel Drive™](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/honda-awd/) standard on upper trims. The hybrid system offered on the Sport and Sport Touring trims features two electric motors, which make these models the most powerful CR-V models ever with an impressive 247 lb-ft of torque.

### MSRP

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V price gets a bit of an increase over 2022, but remains budget-friendly. There are two standard gas-powered CR-V trims and two hybrid trims for 2023. The pricing for the CR-V hybrid models has yet to be released, but you can review the 2023 Honda CR-V price for each of the gas-powered models below: 
        *   **2023 Honda CR-V EX:** Starting MSRP of $31,110**
        *   **2023 Honda CR-V EX-L:** Starting MSRP of $33,760**

## 2023 Honda CR-V MPG

The impressive 2023 Honda CR-V fuel efficiency will allow you to spend more time on the road and less time at the pump. The 2023 Honda CR-V mpg ratings will differ depending on whether it is equipped with the standard rear-wheel drive or the available all-wheel drive.
*   **2023 Honda CR-V MPG – RWD:**28 city/34 highway/30 combined*
*   **2023 Honda CR-V MPG – AWD:** 27 city/32 highway/29 combined*

Part of the reason for these strong 2023 Honda CR-V fuel economy returns is its finely-tuned engine, but additional features such as the Eco Assist™ System and smooth shifting Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) help to conserve fuel consumption.

The 2023 Honda CR-V fuel efficiency numbers for the hybrid models will help you to get even better gas mileage on Jersey City roads and beyond:

*   **2023 Honda CR-V Hybrid MPG** – RWD: 43 city/36 highway/40 combined*
*   **2023 Honda CR-V Hybrid MPG** – AWD: 40 city/34 highway/37 combined*

![Image 10: 2023 Honda CR-V on dusty road](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964337)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Towing Capacity

The Honda CR-V redesign offers improved performance, and with that comes a robust 2023 Honda CR-V towing capacity. How much can a 2023 Honda CR-V tow? With the 2023 Honda CR-V **towing capacity for the gas-powered models is 1,500 pounds**. This will allow you to haul:

*   A small teardrop camper
*   An ATV
*   A jet ski
*   A small fishing boat

While the 2022 CR-V Hybrid was not rated for towing, the redesigned and more powerful 2023 edition can deliver a **hybrid towing capacity of 1,000 pounds**.

There is no specific 2023 Honda CR-V towing package offered, however you can get the following towing accessories in our [Parts Center](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/order-parts/):

*   Drawbar
*   Retaining pin
*   Clip
*   Trailer hitch ball (comes in the 2-inch size or 1 ⅞-inch size)
*   Honda CR-V tow hitch (commonly known as the “trailer hitch harness”)

![Image 11: 2023 Honda CR-V Interior ](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964339)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Interior

The modern design of the 2023 Honda CR-V interior features a **honeycomb dash insert** similar to that offered in the new [**2023 HR-V**](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/2023-hr-v/). As we mentioned previously, the larger 2023 Honda CR-V exterior dimensions increase the interior space. Just how spacious is the 2023 Honda CR-V interior? The maximum seating capacity of up to five remains unchanged from the previous model, however t he 2023 CR-V interior now offers:

*   More cargo space with 36.3 cubic feet available behind the rear seats in both turbocharged (+1.2 cubic feet) and hybrid (+3.1 cubic feet) models.
*   In EX and EX-L models, the rear load floor can be lowered, expanding the cargo space to 39.3 cubic feet. With the 60/40-split rear seatbacks folded flat, cargo space expands to an impressive 76.5 cubic feet.

The available 2023 Honda CR-V interior colors will help you enjoy a sophisticated ambiance with the cabin as you cruise the streets in and around Jersey City:

*   **CR-V EX:**Features gray or black cloth upholstery with an 8-way power driver’s seat and black trim on the dash.
*   **CR-V EX-L:**Adds gray or black leather seating surfaces, a 4-way power passenger seat and piano black dash trim.
*   **CR-V Sport:** Comes with exclusive black cloth upholstery and black dash trim
*   **CR-V Sport Touring:** Offers a choice of either black or gray leather seating surfaces and piano-black dash trim.

# 2023 Honda CR-V Specs

![Image 9: 2023 Honda CR-V](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964334)  
 The [Honda CR-V](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/) has been one of the most popular vehicles in its class for quite a while now, offering drivers sporty performance, a comfortable and versatile cabin space, and a wide array of convenient features. But Honda is always innovating, and with the redesigned next-generation 2023 CR-V, Bayonne-area drivers can expect even more from this well-rounded and fun-to-drive SUV. Learn all about the 2023 Honda CR-V specs, price, and features in this guide from Metro Honda, then check out our [new Honda inventory](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/) in Jersey City today, as well as the recent redesign, fuel economy, and towing capacity!

[New CR-V Inventory](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/)[Continue Your Honda Research](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/manufacturer-information/)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Redesign

Here are some of the highlights of the 2023 Honda CR-V specs:

### Exterior Styling

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V has been redesigned to offer a bold profile that is both rugged and refined with a **large black mesh grille** that is reminiscent of the [Honda Ridgeline](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/search/new-honda-jersey-city-nj/?cy=07305&tp=new/). The Sport and Sport Touring hybrid models receive an even more striking refresh of the front and rear fascia, befitting their sporty performance capabilities.

### Larger, Inside and Out

*       *   One thing Newark-area drivers are sure to notice is that the 2023 Honda CR-V is bigger than the previous edition. In fact, the 2023 CR-V is **2.7 inches long and close to a half inch wider**. In addition, the 1.6 inches added to the wheelbase has resulted in more interior space, especially for rear seat passengers.

### Revised Body Structure

*       *   Along with the styling upgrades, the 2023 Honda CR-V has been built to be **15% stiffer torsionally**, which boosts performance, efficiency, and safety.

### Interior Features

*       *   The modern interior design of the 2023 Honda CR-V features a **honeycomb dash insert** similar to that offered in the new [2023 HR-V](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/2023-hr-v/). As we mentioned previously, the larger proportions of the 2023 CR-V increase the interior space, with the rear legroom expanding by about half an inch. A **standard 7-inch touchscreen** includes [Android Auto™ and Apple CarPlay®](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/connect-to-apple-carplay-android-auto/) capability, while upper trims come with a 9-inch display with wireless smartphone integration. You will also be able to look forward to the advanced driver-assist systems offered with the standard [Honda Sensing®](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/what-is-honda-sensing/).

### Performance

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V specs include t**wo available powertrains: a standard internal combustion engine and a hybrid system**. The gas-powered model will be equipped with a turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and a revised continuously variable transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive is standard on the entry-level model, with [Real Time All-Wheel Drive™](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/honda-awd/) standard on upper trims. The hybrid system offered on the Sport and Sport Touring trims features two electric motors, which make these models the most powerful CR-V models ever with an impressive 247 lb-ft of torque.

### MSRP

*       *   The 2023 Honda CR-V price gets a bit of an increase over 2022, but remains budget-friendly. There are two standard gas-powered CR-V trims and two hybrid trims for 2023. The pricing for the CR-V hybrid models has yet to be released, but you can review the 2023 Honda CR-V price for each of the gas-powered models below: 
        *   **2023 Honda CR-V EX:** Starting MSRP of $31,110**
        *   **2023 Honda CR-V EX-L:** Starting MSRP of $33,760**

## 2023 Honda CR-V MPG

The impressive 2023 Honda CR-V fuel efficiency will allow you to spend more time on the road and less time at the pump. The 2023 Honda CR-V mpg ratings will differ depending on whether it is equipped with the standard rear-wheel drive or the available all-wheel drive.
*   **2023 Honda CR-V MPG – RWD:**28 city/34 highway/30 combined*
*   **2023 Honda CR-V MPG – AWD:** 27 city/32 highway/29 combined*

Part of the reason for these strong 2023 Honda CR-V fuel economy returns is its finely-tuned engine, but additional features such as the Eco Assist™ System and smooth shifting Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) help to conserve fuel consumption.

The 2023 Honda CR-V fuel efficiency numbers for the hybrid models will help you to get even better gas mileage on Jersey City roads and beyond:

*   **2023 Honda CR-V Hybrid MPG** – RWD: 43 city/36 highway/40 combined*
*   **2023 Honda CR-V Hybrid MPG** – AWD: 40 city/34 highway/37 combined*

![Image 10: 2023 Honda CR-V on dusty road](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964337)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Towing Capacity

The Honda CR-V redesign offers improved performance, and with that comes a robust 2023 Honda CR-V towing capacity. How much can a 2023 Honda CR-V tow? With the 2023 Honda CR-V **towing capacity for the gas-powered models is 1,500 pounds**. This will allow you to haul:

*   A small teardrop camper
*   An ATV
*   A jet ski
*   A small fishing boat

While the 2022 CR-V Hybrid was not rated for towing, the redesigned and more powerful 2023 edition can deliver a **hybrid towing capacity of 1,000 pounds**.

There is no specific 2023 Honda CR-V towing package offered, however you can get the following towing accessories in our [Parts Center](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/order-parts/):

*   Drawbar
*   Retaining pin
*   Clip
*   Trailer hitch ball (comes in the 2-inch size or 1 ⅞-inch size)
*   Honda CR-V tow hitch (commonly known as the “trailer hitch harness”)

![Image 11: 2023 Honda CR-V Interior ](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/2964339)

## 2023 Honda CR-V Interior

The modern design of the 2023 Honda CR-V interior features a **honeycomb dash insert** similar to that offered in the new [**2023 HR-V**](https://www.mymetrohonda.com/2023-hr-v/). As we mentioned previously, the larger 2023 Honda CR-V exterior dimensions increase the interior space. Just how spacious is the 2023 Honda CR-V interior? The maximum seating capacity of up to five remains unchanged from the previous model, however t he 2023 CR-V interior now offers:

*   More cargo space with 36.3 cubic feet available behind the rear seats in both turbocharged (+1.2 cubic feet) and hybrid (+3.1 cubic feet) models.
*   In EX and EX-L models, the rear load floor can be lowered, expanding the cargo space to 39.3 cubic feet. With the 60/40-split rear seatbacks folded flat, cargo space expands to an impressive 76.5 cubic feet.

The available 2023 Honda CR-V interior colors will help you enjoy a sophisticated ambiance with the cabin as you cruise the streets in and around Jersey City:

*   **CR-V Sport Touring:** Offers a choice of either black or gray leather seating surfaces and piano-black dash trim.

## 2023 Honda HR-V Review

[![Image 7: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   Spacious cabin
*   Honda quality
*   Lots of safety features

### Cons

*   No hybrid variant
*   Magic Seat has disappeared

### What's New?

*   This is an all-new generation
*   Now based on the Civic
*   More power than before

One of the best subcompact SUVs is updated. The 2023 Honda HR-V becomes even more compelling and refined. [Honda](https://www.kbb.com/honda/) builds this [second-generation model](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2023-honda-hr-v-appears-improved-suv-on-civic-bones/) on the same platform as the current Civic, which only launched last year (the original HR-V was based on the little Fit hatchback).

That means a more sophisticated suspension for better ride quality, plus a keener engine. The new HR-V is also completely contemporary inside and out. Safety tech starts quite generously, but spending a little more for blind-spot monitoring and a few extra features is a good idea.

The previous Honda HR-V never got accused of being too powerful. The new 2023 HR-V comes with 158 horsepower and 138 lb-ft of torque — a noticeable improvement over 141 horsepower and 127 lb-ft of thrust. While there’s a slight decrease in fuel efficiency compared to the former model, this new HR-V averages 28 mpg combined with front-wheel drive, so it’s a bearable trade-off for the added power.

Active noise cancellation is standard, and the previous torsion beam rear suspension has been replaced by a multi-link setup offering greater comfort and control. All-wheel drive is available, and hill descent control is standard in every new HR-V. Just like its predecessor, though, this subcompact SUV doesn’t have any serious off-road talent. Those who live in colder regions will nevertheless appreciate the value of having four driven wheels

### 2023 Honda HR-V Pricing

2023 Honda HR-V pricing starts at $21,300 for the HR-V LX Sport Utility 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $25,125 when new. The range-topping 2023 HR-V EX-L Sport Utility 4D starts at $25,700 today, originally priced from $30,725.

### Driving the Honda HR-V

_KBB’s Micah Muzio [drove a new HR-V](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/first-drive-2023-honda-hr-v/) recently in Oregon. Reports Micah:_

The HR-V drives with more sophistication than its price would suggest, lending itself to pleasing commutes. But is there any fun to be extracted along the way? Yes. The HR-V corners with confidence, and there’s just a splash of sportiness, aided by steering that has a satisfying heft and predictability.

At full-throttle, the HR-V feels peppy. And truth be told, the continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) works great. While CVTs routinely are criticized for creating an elastic acceleration curve accompanied by a racing engine, Honda’s CVT feels a lot like a conventional automatic. Most folks will have no idea it’s a CVT.

Other random observations: The outward view from the HR-V’s driver’s seat is good, cabin noise at highway speeds is more than tolerable, and unfortunately there are no vents for the rear seat. And while I miss the former HR-V’s cleverly folding Magic Seat, I do like how the new small key fob minimizes bulk in your pockets. What’s more, the HR-V’s lane-keeping assist feature does an exceptional job keeping the HR-V in its lane, but I found the adaptive cruise control to be a bit slow in adapting to the changing speed of the vehicle ahead.

All told, the new HR-V feels more substantive than the vehicle it replaces, and I like how each trim has a flavor of its own. In fact, the elevated aura of the new 2023 Honda HR-V relates directly to its improved interiors.

### Interior Comfort

The magic has gone — in a certain sense. The previous HR-V had a Magic Seat behind the first row where the bottom cushions could flip up and contribute to cargo-carrying versatility. Honda fits a set of typical 60/40 split-folding rear seats into the 2023 HR-V. They can still fold flat to create an extremely useful load space, but who doesn’t want a Magic Seat?

Elsewhere in [the new HR-V’s cabin](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2023-honda-hr-v-interior/), some magic carries over. There’s the usual Honda fit and finish, and an increasingly common minimalist approach to the dashboard — with controls migrating to the touchscreen and/or the steering wheel.

A more maximalist approach applies to rear legroom: 37.7 inches. That’s one of the best in this subcompact SUV class, although slightly less than the old HR-V. Luggage space behind the rear seats measures 24.4 cubic feet. Maximum cargo area with the rear seats folded is 55.1 cubic feet. The [Kia Seltos](https://www.kbb.com/kia/seltos/2023/)has more, but the HR-V is another class standout.

**2023 Subcompact SUV Roominess**

![Image 8: Honda HR-V cargo volume and legroom compared to other subcompact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/CargoAndLegRoom_HondaHR-V.png)

### Exterior Styling

New generation, new look. The 2023 HR-V loses the designed-by-committee vibe and puts forward a more distinct appearance.

Because of its Civic foundation, the new HR-V not-so-subcompact SUV is bigger than before. Its wheelbase (the distance between the front and rear axles) expands by nearly 2 inches. Width grows by about 2.5 inches. And overall length is greater by almost 9.5 inches.

The alloy wheels of the LX are painted silver, the Sport’s rims are gloss black (matched by a grille, side mirror housings, and rear spoiler also in gloss black), and the EX-L’s alloys are machine-finished with inserts of Gloss Shark Gray. Premium paint choices are Nordic Forest Pearl, Platinum White Pearl, and Urban Gray Pearl.

### Favorite Features

HONDALINK  
 Download the HondaLink app onto a smartphone, and a range of services becomes available, such as stolen vehicle location, geofencing, automatic collision notification, and service appointments. This is standard with every new HR-V SUV.

SMART ENTRY WITH WALK AWAY AUTO LOCK  
 “Did I lock the car?” This question invariably springs to mind just as your plane takes off and you see all the long-term parking lots becoming smaller. With this feature, standard in the top two trims, such angst becomes a thing of the past.

### Standard Features

The introductory LX trim of the new HR-V subcompact SUV is not exactly overflowing with standard features, but it does have a decent amount of driver aids — forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, lane-departure warning/lane-keeping assistance, adaptive cruise control with low-speed follow, Traffic Jam Assist, and automatic high beams.

The rest of the inventory includes 17-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights/daytime running lights/brake lights, single-zone automatic climate control, and cloth upholstery. The infotainment system has a 7-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto smartphone integration, three USB ports, Bluetooth, and four speakers.

### Factory Options

Except for all-wheel drive, the way to acquire more equipment in a 2023 HR-V is to select a higher trim, rather than cherry pick from a list of options. Sport trim is a couple of grand more than LX, adding 18-inch alloy wheels, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, keyless entry/ignition with Walk Away Auto Lock, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and heated front seats.

[EX-L](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2022-honda-hr-v-fully-loaded/) reverts to 17-inch alloy wheels and brings low-speed braking control, powered moonroof, front/rear parking sensors, dual-zone automatic climate control, 8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, leather seating surfaces, self-dimming rearview mirror, ambient LED cabin lighting, turn-by-turn directions, 9-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, wireless charging, satellite radio, and an 8-speaker/180-watt audio system.

### Engine & Transmission

One engine covers all three new HR-V trim levels. It’s a 2.0-liter 4-cylinder unit without any turbocharging.

Output is 158 horsepower and 138 lb-ft of torque. This connects to an automatic continuously variable transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive (FWD) is standard. All-wheel drive (AWD) is optional across the lineup. Regular gasoline is perfectly acceptable.

2.0-liter inline-4  
 158 horsepower @ 6,500 rpm  
 138 lb-ft of torque @ 4,200 rpm  
 EPA city/highway fuel economy: 26/32 mpg (FWD), 25/30 mpg (AWD)

More HR-Vfuel economy information is available at the [EPA’s website](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/make.shtml).

### **Excellent Safety Scores**

The 2023 Honda HR-V is an [IIHS Top Safety Pick+](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/vehicle/honda/hr-v-4-door-suv/2023) thanks to its good crash test scores and a generous list of standard safety features.

### **3-Year/36,000-Mile Warranty**

The Honda HR-V is covered by a 3-year/36,000-mile basic warranty and a 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty. This coverage is average for this class, but you also get complimentary scheduled maintenance for two years or 24,000 miles.

It features advanced safety functions, including Advanced Cruise Control with low-speed follow and lane-keep assist, which allows you to keep your foot off the pedals for a considerable distance, as it will slow and even come to a complete stop (although it is not recommended to rely on this feature at high speeds when stopping sooner is necessary). The keyless entry feature is also nice, and self-locks once the remote is a certain distance away. Overall, a wonderful car, and I'm very happy with my purchase.

## 2023 Honda HR-V Safety

### Safety Features & Technology

### **Honda Sensing**

This set of driver assistance features is standard in every new HR-V SUV, adding the now-usual things like forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking and pedestrian detection, plus road departure mitigation, lane-keeping assistance, and automatic high beams.

### **Traffic Jam Assist**

Another part of the Honda Sensing array, along with adaptive cruise control system and Low-Speed Follow. Traffic Jam Assist provides minor steering corrections to keep the 2023 HR-V in its lane.

### **Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert**

Becoming standard at the Sport level, this system warns the driver of any vehicles approaching either in adjacent lanes or from right angles when reversing out of a parking spot.

## FAQs

#### How much is a 2023 Honda HR-V?

Prices for the 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV start at $23,800 and go up to $27,900. This is all before any options or destination charges.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V a good SUV?

From the bare bones to the outer skin, virtually everything about the all-new 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV is a step up from the already excellent first-generation version.

#### Does the 2023 Honda HR-V have all-wheel drive?

All-wheel drive is available as an option in the 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV with any of the three trim levels. The extra cost is $1,500.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V a good vehicle?

Yes, the 2023 Honda HR-V is a good car, as reflected by its above-average Kelley Blue Book rating of 4.7 out of 5.

#### What is the MPG for a 2023 Honda HR-V?

2023 Honda HR-V city/highway fuel economy ratings range from 25/30 mpg to 26/32 mpg, depending on trim and equipment.

#### How much should a 2023 Honda HR-V cost?

Used 2023 Honda HR-V prices currently range from $21,300 for the LX Sport Utility 4D to $25,700 for the EX-L Sport Utility 4D when purchasing from a dealership, depending on a range of factors like equipment, mileage, and condition.

#### What's the cheapest Honda HR-V?

The cheapest 2023 Honda HR-V is the LX Sport Utility 4D, with a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $21,300.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V reliable?

The 2023 Honda HR-V is part of the 2nd-generation HR-V, which our owners give an above-average reliability rating of 4.4 out of 5.

## 2023 Honda HR-V Review

[![Image 7: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   Spacious cabin
*   Honda quality
*   Lots of safety features

### Cons

*   No hybrid variant
*   Magic Seat has disappeared

### What's New?

*   This is an all-new generation
*   Now based on the Civic
*   More power than before

One of the best subcompact SUVs is updated. The 2023 Honda HR-V becomes even more compelling and refined. [Honda](https://www.kbb.com/honda/) builds this [second-generation model](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2023-honda-hr-v-appears-improved-suv-on-civic-bones/) on the same platform as the current Civic, which only launched last year (the original HR-V was based on the little Fit hatchback).

That means a more sophisticated suspension for better ride quality, plus a keener engine. The new HR-V is also completely contemporary inside and out. Safety tech starts quite generously, but spending a little more for blind-spot monitoring and a few extra features is a good idea.

The previous Honda HR-V never got accused of being too powerful. The new 2023 HR-V comes with 158 horsepower and 138 lb-ft of torque — a noticeable improvement over 141 horsepower and 127 lb-ft of thrust. While there’s a slight decrease in fuel efficiency compared to the former model, this new HR-V averages 28 mpg combined with front-wheel drive, so it’s a bearable trade-off for the added power.

Active noise cancellation is standard, and the previous torsion beam rear suspension has been replaced by a multi-link setup offering greater comfort and control. All-wheel drive is available, and hill descent control is standard in every new HR-V. Just like its predecessor, though, this subcompact SUV doesn’t have any serious off-road talent. Those who live in colder regions will nevertheless appreciate the value of having four driven wheels

### 2023 Honda HR-V Pricing

2023 Honda HR-V pricing starts at $21,300 for the HR-V LX Sport Utility 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $25,125 when new. The range-topping 2023 HR-V EX-L Sport Utility 4D starts at $25,700 today, originally priced from $30,725.

### Driving the Honda HR-V

_KBB’s Micah Muzio [drove a new HR-V](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/first-drive-2023-honda-hr-v/) recently in Oregon. Reports Micah:_

The HR-V drives with more sophistication than its price would suggest, lending itself to pleasing commutes. But is there any fun to be extracted along the way? Yes. The HR-V corners with confidence, and there’s just a splash of sportiness, aided by steering that has a satisfying heft and predictability.

At full-throttle, the HR-V feels peppy. And truth be told, the continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) works great. While CVTs routinely are criticized for creating an elastic acceleration curve accompanied by a racing engine, Honda’s CVT feels a lot like a conventional automatic. Most folks will have no idea it’s a CVT.

Other random observations: The outward view from the HR-V’s driver’s seat is good, cabin noise at highway speeds is more than tolerable, and unfortunately there are no vents for the rear seat. And while I miss the former HR-V’s cleverly folding Magic Seat, I do like how the new small key fob minimizes bulk in your pockets. What’s more, the HR-V’s lane-keeping assist feature does an exceptional job keeping the HR-V in its lane, but I found the adaptive cruise control to be a bit slow in adapting to the changing speed of the vehicle ahead.

All told, the new HR-V feels more substantive than the vehicle it replaces, and I like how each trim has a flavor of its own. In fact, the elevated aura of the new 2023 Honda HR-V relates directly to its improved interiors.

### Interior Comfort

The magic has gone — in a certain sense. The previous HR-V had a Magic Seat behind the first row where the bottom cushions could flip up and contribute to cargo-carrying versatility. Honda fits a set of typical 60/40 split-folding rear seats into the 2023 HR-V. They can still fold flat to create an extremely useful load space, but who doesn’t want a Magic Seat?

Elsewhere in [the new HR-V’s cabin](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2023-honda-hr-v-interior/), some magic carries over. There’s the usual Honda fit and finish, and an increasingly common minimalist approach to the dashboard — with controls migrating to the touchscreen and/or the steering wheel.

A more maximalist approach applies to rear legroom: 37.7 inches. That’s one of the best in this subcompact SUV class, although slightly less than the old HR-V. Luggage space behind the rear seats measures 24.4 cubic feet. Maximum cargo area with the rear seats folded is 55.1 cubic feet. The [Kia Seltos](https://www.kbb.com/kia/seltos/2023/)has more, but the HR-V is another class standout.

**2023 Subcompact SUV Roominess**

![Image 8: Honda HR-V cargo volume and legroom compared to other subcompact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/CargoAndLegRoom_HondaHR-V.png)

### Exterior Styling

New generation, new look. The 2023 HR-V loses the designed-by-committee vibe and puts forward a more distinct appearance.

Because of its Civic foundation, the new HR-V not-so-subcompact SUV is bigger than before. Its wheelbase (the distance between the front and rear axles) expands by nearly 2 inches. Width grows by about 2.5 inches. And overall length is greater by almost 9.5 inches.

The alloy wheels of the LX are painted silver, the Sport’s rims are gloss black (matched by a grille, side mirror housings, and rear spoiler also in gloss black), and the EX-L’s alloys are machine-finished with inserts of Gloss Shark Gray. Premium paint choices are Nordic Forest Pearl, Platinum White Pearl, and Urban Gray Pearl.

### Favorite Features

HONDALINK  
 Download the HondaLink app onto a smartphone, and a range of services becomes available, such as stolen vehicle location, geofencing, automatic collision notification, and service appointments. This is standard with every new HR-V SUV.

SMART ENTRY WITH WALK AWAY AUTO LOCK  
 “Did I lock the car?” This question invariably springs to mind just as your plane takes off and you see all the long-term parking lots becoming smaller. With this feature, standard in the top two trims, such angst becomes a thing of the past.

### Standard Features

The introductory LX trim of the new HR-V subcompact SUV is not exactly overflowing with standard features, but it does have a decent amount of driver aids — forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, lane-departure warning/lane-keeping assistance, adaptive cruise control with low-speed follow, Traffic Jam Assist, and automatic high beams.

The rest of the inventory includes 17-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights/daytime running lights/brake lights, single-zone automatic climate control, and cloth upholstery. The infotainment system has a 7-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto smartphone integration, three USB ports, Bluetooth, and four speakers.

### Factory Options

Except for all-wheel drive, the way to acquire more equipment in a 2023 HR-V is to select a higher trim, rather than cherry pick from a list of options. Sport trim is a couple of grand more than LX, adding 18-inch alloy wheels, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, keyless entry/ignition with Walk Away Auto Lock, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and heated front seats.

[EX-L](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/2022-honda-hr-v-fully-loaded/) reverts to 17-inch alloy wheels and brings low-speed braking control, powered moonroof, front/rear parking sensors, dual-zone automatic climate control, 8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, leather seating surfaces, self-dimming rearview mirror, ambient LED cabin lighting, turn-by-turn directions, 9-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, wireless charging, satellite radio, and an 8-speaker/180-watt audio system.

### Engine & Transmission

One engine covers all three new HR-V trim levels. It’s a 2.0-liter 4-cylinder unit without any turbocharging.

Output is 158 horsepower and 138 lb-ft of torque. This connects to an automatic continuously variable transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive (FWD) is standard. All-wheel drive (AWD) is optional across the lineup. Regular gasoline is perfectly acceptable.

More HR-Vfuel economy information is available at the [EPA’s website](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/make.shtml).

### **Excellent Safety Scores**

The 2023 Honda HR-V is an [IIHS Top Safety Pick+](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/vehicle/honda/hr-v-4-door-suv/2023) thanks to its good crash test scores and a generous list of standard safety features.

### **3-Year/36,000-Mile Warranty**

The Honda HR-V is covered by a 3-year/36,000-mile basic warranty and a 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty. This coverage is average for this class, but you also get complimentary scheduled maintenance for two years or 24,000 miles.

## 2023 Honda HR-V Safety

### Safety Features & Technology

### **Honda Sensing**

This set of driver assistance features is standard in every new HR-V SUV, adding the now-usual things like forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking and pedestrian detection, plus road departure mitigation, lane-keeping assistance, and automatic high beams.

### **Traffic Jam Assist**

Another part of the Honda Sensing array, along with adaptive cruise control system and Low-Speed Follow. Traffic Jam Assist provides minor steering corrections to keep the 2023 HR-V in its lane.

### **Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert**

Becoming standard at the Sport level, this system warns the driver of any vehicles approaching either in adjacent lanes or from right angles when reversing out of a parking spot.

## FAQs

#### How much is a 2023 Honda HR-V?

Prices for the 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV start at $23,800 and go up to $27,900. This is all before any options or destination charges.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V a good SUV?

From the bare bones to the outer skin, virtually everything about the all-new 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV is a step up from the already excellent first-generation version.

#### Does the 2023 Honda HR-V have all-wheel drive?

All-wheel drive is available as an option in the 2023 HR-V subcompact SUV with any of the three trim levels. The extra cost is $1,500.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V a good vehicle?

Yes, the 2023 Honda HR-V is a good car, as reflected by its above-average Kelley Blue Book rating of 4.7 out of 5.

#### What is the MPG for a 2023 Honda HR-V?

2023 Honda HR-V city/highway fuel economy ratings range from 25/30 mpg to 26/32 mpg, depending on trim and equipment.

#### How much should a 2023 Honda HR-V cost?

Used 2023 Honda HR-V prices currently range from $21,300 for the LX Sport Utility 4D to $25,700 for the EX-L Sport Utility 4D when purchasing from a dealership, depending on a range of factors like equipment, mileage, and condition.

#### What's the cheapest Honda HR-V?

The cheapest 2023 Honda HR-V is the LX Sport Utility 4D, with a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $21,300.

#### Is the 2023 Honda HR-V reliable?

The 2023 Honda HR-V is part of the 2nd-generation HR-V, which our owners give an above-average reliability rating of 4.4 out of 5.

## 2027 Honda HR-V Review

[![Image 6: Robert Duffer](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/2e2eb78f6ccecefccf836fb8d98a06459e1ccb849a5879198f216103a30d3da4?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/robert-duffer/)

By [Robert Duffer](https://www.kbb.com/author/robert-duffer/)

Updated August 07, 2026

Robert Duffer has covered the automotive industry since 2013. As the automotive editor at the Chicago Tribune, Duffer managed print and online content, and his weekly automotive column was syndicated to 140 markets nationwide. Shifting gears to Senior Editor at The Car Connection, Motor Authority, and Green Car Reports, Duffer amassed thousands of bylines ranging from executive interviews to minivan reviews. Duffer is currently Editor II at KBB.com and Autotrader. His favorite car is the next one. A frequent podcast and radio guest, as well as an award-winning creative writer and teacher, Duffer has written for media such as the New York Times, Forbes, National Public Radio, and others.

### Pros

*   Small yet spacious
*   Smart interior
*   Good standard features

### Cons

*   Single, sluggish powertrain
*   No hybrid option

### What's New?

*   Unchanged after its 2026 refresh

**The 2027 Honda HR-V stands out as a small yet spacious SUV, highlighted by a pedigree big on reliability and value. Pricing starts at $28,050.**

Refreshed last year with more standard features that include a 9-inch touchscreen and wireless device charging, the Honda HR-V subcompact SUV rolls on as a great buy loaded with standard safety and convenience features. Redesigned in 2023 and related to the Honda Civic, the HR-V lacks the Civic’s hybrid option, unfortunately, but does offer all-wheel drive. The interior is optimized for space with a tiered console, deep door pockets, and a relatively large cargo hold.

_We’ve logged hundreds of hours driving and evaluating this generation_ _[subcompact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/suv/best-subcompact-suvs/), including the Honda HR-V._

The front-wheel-drive HR-V can be equipped with all-wheel drive (AWD) for $1,500 on each of its three trims. Rivals such as the Chevy Trax and Hyundai Venue lack an AWD option, but this crowded subcompact SUV class is loaded with compelling rivals, including the [Mazda CX-30](https://www.kbb.com/mazda/cx-30/),[Toyota Corolla Cross](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/corolla-cross/),[Kia Seltos](https://www.kbb.com/kia/seltos/),[Hyundai Kona](https://www.kbb.com/hyundai/kona/), and the[Subaru Crosstrek](https://www.kbb.com/subaru/crosstrek/). The CX-30 and Crosstrek both come with all-wheel drive as standard. The HR-V costs a bit more than the Nissan Kicks, Chevy Trailblazer, and Toyota Corolla Cross, but it’s still a reasonable value.

Before buying a Honda HR-V, check the Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price to know what you should really pay. Like many[Honda models](https://www.kbb.com/honda/), HR-V resale values are above average for the segment. Recouping more money when selling a vehicle can mean a bigger down payment and lower monthly payments on the next one.

### Driving the Honda HR-V

Driving the HR-V is like going for a walk: It’s calm, pleasant, and unexciting, and if you try and push it, its joints may creak. A 158-horsepower 2.0-liter 4-cylinder motivates things, and a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) balances power and efficiency relatively well, earning an EPA rating of 28 mpg combined with FWD. Hammer the throttle and the powertrain seems to groan in protest, but in normal everyday driving, it’s just fine. The HR-V lacks the verve of the 191-hp CX-30, and the relatively larger size of the Honda makes it a bit heavier and slower.

We’d love to see the 200-hp hybrid powertrain used in the Civic and rated at up to 49 mpg combined put into the HR-V, though it would drive up the price. The Civic Sport Hybrid sedan costs $2,700 more than the Civic Sport.

Like the Civic, the steering feel is nicely weighted, and the HR-V handles with more agility than the larger CR-V. It’s relatively quiet and composed on the highway, but it’s easy to park and has excellent outward vision.

**Powertrain**

**Engine****HP/Torque****Transmission****MPG (comb.)**
2.0-liter inline-4 158 hp/138 lb-ft CVT 28 mpg FWD/27 AWD

### Interior Comfort

The HR-V adopts the Civic’s mesh vent panels and horizontal dash layout. There’s a lot of black but it’s mostly soft to the touch. Climate dials and buttons are a nice antidote for too-much touchscreen. Active noise cancellation and an acoustic windshield give it a bit more refinement than most rivals.

We’ve mentioned a few of the space-optimizing design elements such as the tiered center console, but by the tape, the HR-V measures up as one of the roomiest in the class. It has 37.7 inches of rear legroom, barely trailing the Chevy Trailblazer, Jeep Compass, and Hyundai Kona. Cargo room is a similar story, with 24.4 cubic feet behind the rear seats. There’s plenty of space for four adults, and a fifth could squeeze in for a road trip home from college, say.

### Favorite Features

**Tiered Console**

The Honda HR-V is larger than some rivals, and the interior space is optimized to make the most out of it. The standard wireless device charger sits below the climate control panel, and cupholders separate it from the gear shifter. The console narrows into a thin band with a drive mode selector and a few other functions, which all hover over an open recess with USB-C ports to stow or charge other devices. Deep door pockets also reflect the great use of space.

**Good Standard Features**

Last year introduced a 9-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard, as well as wireless device charging. That last bit is unusual in this cost-sensitive segment. The HR-V also has conveniences such as adaptive cruise control and active noise cancellation.

**High-Value Sport Trim**

For $1,800 more than the base LX, the mid-grade Sport strikes as the best value. It upgrades from 17- to 18-inch wheels, and adds heated front seats, a leather-wrapped steering wheel and shifter, remote start, gloss-black exterior trim, blind-spot monitoring, and Smart Lock, which means you don’t have to take out the fob or your app to unlock and lock the doors on approach.

Keyless Entry, Advanced Cruise Control, Lane Keep Assist, Comfortable, Good on Gas

Cons

Steering recall, Easily breakable air vent slats, trunk seal sometimes squeaks on bumpy roads

I bought a 2023 Honda HR-V LX about a week ago, and so far nothing but positive things to say. Although a bit smaller than the CR-Vs, there is plenty of space for everyday driving as well as groceries (even at Sam's Club). The design is sleek and relatively minimalistic. It has enough legroom for both the driver and all passengers, sizable trunk space, and just enough power ports for most needs, including a 12V car outlet in the trunk for tire pumps, additional plugs, etc. I love the CarPlay feature, though I wish it didn't require a USB connection. It features advanced safety functions, including Advanced Cruise Control with low-speed follow and lane-keep assist, which allows you to keep your foot off the pedals for a considerable distance, as it will slow and even come to a complete stop (although it is not recommended to rely on this feature at high speeds when stopping sooner is necessary). The keyless entry feature is also nice, and self-locks once the remote is a certain distance away. Overall, a wonderful car, and I'm very happy with my purchase.

## 2027 Honda HR-V Review

[![Image 6: Robert Duffer](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/2e2eb78f6ccecefccf836fb8d98a06459e1ccb849a5879198f216103a30d3da4?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/robert-duffer/)
