### Pros

*   Small yet spacious
*   Smart interior
*   Good standard features

### Cons

*   Single, sluggish powertrain
*   No hybrid option

### What's New?

*   Unchanged after its 2026 refresh

**The 2027 Honda HR-V stands out as a small yet spacious SUV, highlighted by a pedigree big on reliability and value. Pricing starts at $28,050.**

Refreshed last year with more standard features that include a 9-inch touchscreen and wireless device charging, the Honda HR-V subcompact SUV rolls on as a great buy loaded with standard safety and convenience features. Redesigned in 2023 and related to the Honda Civic, the HR-V lacks the Civic’s hybrid option, unfortunately, but does offer all-wheel drive. The interior is optimized for space with a tiered console, deep door pockets, and a relatively large cargo hold.

_We’ve logged hundreds of hours driving and evaluating this generation_ _[subcompact SUVs](https://www.kbb.com/suv/best-subcompact-suvs/), including the Honda HR-V._

The front-wheel-drive HR-V can be equipped with all-wheel drive (AWD) for $1,500 on each of its three trims. Rivals such as the Chevy Trax and Hyundai Venue lack an AWD option, but this crowded subcompact SUV class is loaded with compelling rivals, including the [Mazda CX-30](https://www.kbb.com/mazda/cx-30/),[Toyota Corolla Cross](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/corolla-cross/),[Kia Seltos](https://www.kbb.com/kia/seltos/),[Hyundai Kona](https://www.kbb.com/hyundai/kona/), and the[Subaru Crosstrek](https://www.kbb.com/subaru/crosstrek/). The CX-30 and Crosstrek both come with all-wheel drive as standard. The HR-V costs a bit more than the Nissan Kicks, Chevy Trailblazer, and Toyota Corolla Cross, but it’s still a reasonable value.

Before buying a Honda HR-V, check the Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price to know what you should really pay. Like many[Honda models](https://www.kbb.com/honda/), HR-V resale values are above average for the segment. Recouping more money when selling a vehicle can mean a bigger down payment and lower monthly payments on the next one.

### Driving the Honda HR-V

Driving the HR-V is like going for a walk: It’s calm, pleasant, and unexciting, and if you try and push it, its joints may creak. A 158-horsepower 2.0-liter 4-cylinder motivates things, and a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) balances power and efficiency relatively well, earning an EPA rating of 28 mpg combined with FWD. Hammer the throttle and the powertrain seems to groan in protest, but in normal everyday driving, it’s just fine. The HR-V lacks the verve of the 191-hp CX-30, and the relatively larger size of the Honda makes it a bit heavier and slower.

We’d love to see the 200-hp hybrid powertrain used in the Civic and rated at up to 49 mpg combined put into the HR-V, though it would drive up the price. The Civic Sport Hybrid sedan costs $2,700 more than the Civic Sport.

Like the Civic, the steering feel is nicely weighted, and the HR-V handles with more agility than the larger CR-V. It’s relatively quiet and composed on the highway, but it’s easy to park and has excellent outward vision.

### Interior Comfort

The HR-V adopts the Civic’s mesh vent panels and horizontal dash layout. There’s a lot of black but it’s mostly soft to the touch. Climate dials and buttons are a nice antidote for too-much touchscreen. Active noise cancellation and an acoustic windshield give it a bit more refinement than most rivals.

We’ve mentioned a few of the space-optimizing design elements such as the tiered center console, but by the tape, the HR-V measures up as one of the roomiest in the class. It has 37.7 inches of rear legroom, barely trailing the Chevy Trailblazer, Jeep Compass, and Hyundai Kona. Cargo room is a similar story, with 24.4 cubic feet behind the rear seats. There’s plenty of space for four adults, and a fifth could squeeze in for a road trip home from college, say.

### Favorite Features

**Tiered Console**

The Honda HR-V is larger than some rivals, and the interior space is optimized to make the most out of it. The standard wireless device charger sits below the climate control panel, and cupholders separate it from the gear shifter. The console narrows into a thin band with a drive mode selector and a few other functions, which all hover over an open recess with USB-C ports to stow or charge other devices. Deep door pockets also reflect the great use of space.

**Good Standard Features**

Last year introduced a 9-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard, as well as wireless device charging. That last bit is unusual in this cost-sensitive segment. The HR-V also has conveniences such as adaptive cruise control and active noise cancellation.

**High-Value Sport Trim**

For $1,800 more than the base LX, the mid-grade Sport strikes as the best value. It upgrades from 17- to 18-inch wheels, and adds heated front seats, a leather-wrapped steering wheel and shifter, remote start, gloss-black exterior trim, blind-spot monitoring, and Smart Lock, which means you don’t have to take out the fob or your app to unlock and lock the doors on approach.

It features advanced safety functions, including Advanced Cruise Control with low-speed follow and lane-keep assist, which allows you to keep your foot off the pedals for a considerable distance, as it will slow and even come to a complete stop (although it is not recommended to rely on this feature at high speeds when stopping sooner is necessary). * * *

If you’re looking for a versatile SUV with an accommodating interior, the 2023 Honda HR-V is a great choice. The [new Honda HR-V](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/new-vehicles/hr-v/) provides the spacious passenger and cargo areas you need to travel comfortably around Round Rock. Below, you can get a closer look at the 2023 Honda HR-V interior with First Texas Honda, and learn more about its space, design, and features.

[New HR-V Inventory](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/new-vehicles/hr-v/)[Contact Us](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/contact-us/)

## 2023 HR-V Cargo Space

Despite its small size, the Honda HR-V offers ample storage space, allowing you to run errands around San Marcos with ease. With the rear seat up, the Honda HR-V cargo space is slightly less than it is with the seats down. Folding the seats down gives you even more storage space, so you can transport everything in one trip. Compare the Honda HR-V cargo space measurements below:

*   **HR-V Cargo Space (Seat Up)**: 24.4 cubic feet
*   **HR-V Cargo Space (Seat Down)**: 55.1 cubic feet

## 2023 HR-V Seating & Dimensions

The Honda HR-V seating ensures you and your passengers have a comfortable ride through Cedar Park. Inside the cabin, you’ll find features like a 60/40 Split 2nd-Row Magic Seat®, which provides easy access to the cargo area. Here’s a breakdown of the Honda HR-V dimensions and seating room:

*   Front Headroom: 39.4 inches
*   Front Shoulder Room: 56.6 inches
*   Front Hip Room: 54 inches
*   Front Legroom: 41.9 inches
*   Rear Headroom: 47.4 inches
*   Rear Shoulder Room: 55.2 inches
*   Rear Hip Room: 47.4 inches
*   Rear Legroom: 37.7 inches
*   Passenger Volume: 98.7 cubic feet

## 2023 HR-V Interior Design & Features

The Honda HR-V cabin takes comfort a step further by offering plenty of next-level features, as well as generous seating and dimensions. You can take advantage of several of the features to help you save space and store your belongings. Here’s a closer look at some of the highlighted Honda HR-V features:

*   Air Conditioning with Air-Filtration System
*   Illuminated Steering Wheel-Mounted Controls
*   Chrome Door Pulls
*   Cargo Area Tie-Down Anchors
*   High-Deck Center Console with Sliding Armrest and Storage Compartment
*   Cargo Area Light
*   Available Automatic Climate Control
*   Available Heated Front Seats
*   Available Leather Seating

# 2023 Honda HR-V Interior

 October 1st, 2022 by[First Texas Honda](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/author/firsttexashonda_author/ "Posts by First Texas Honda")

 Share this Post: [Share on Facebook](javascript:void(0);)[Share on Twitter](javascript:void(0);)

![Image 7: 2023 Honda HR-V Interior Seating](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/F5U8N7A7hzHzhKuE4JRgJhgIEs34nmCZGDsmJhiz.jpg)

* * *

If you’re looking for a versatile SUV with an accommodating interior, the 2023 Honda HR-V is a great choice. The [new Honda HR-V](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/new-vehicles/hr-v/) provides the spacious passenger and cargo areas you need to travel comfortably around Round Rock. Below, you can get a closer look at the 2023 Honda HR-V interior with First Texas Honda, and learn more about its space, design, and features.

[New HR-V Inventory](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/new-vehicles/hr-v/)[Contact Us](https://www.firsttexashonda.com/contact-us/)

## 2023 HR-V Cargo Space

Despite its small size, the Honda HR-V offers ample storage space, allowing you to run errands around San Marcos with ease. With the rear seat up, the Honda HR-V cargo space is slightly less than it is with the seats down. Folding the seats down gives you even more storage space, so you can transport everything in one trip. Compare the Honda HR-V cargo space measurements below:

*   **HR-V Cargo Space (Seat Up)**: 24.4 cubic feet
*   **HR-V Cargo Space (Seat Down)**: 55.1 cubic feet

## 2023 HR-V Seating & Dimensions

The Honda HR-V seating ensures you and your passengers have a comfortable ride through Cedar Park. Inside the cabin, you’ll find features like a 60/40 Split 2nd-Row Magic Seat®, which provides easy access to the cargo area. Here’s a breakdown of the Honda HR-V dimensions and seating room:

*   Front Headroom: 39.4 inches
*   Front Shoulder Room: 56.6 inches
*   Front Hip Room: 54 inches
*   Front Legroom: 41.9 inches
*   Rear Headroom: 47.4 inches
*   Rear Shoulder Room: 55.2 inches
*   Rear Hip Room: 47.4 inches
*   Rear Legroom: 37.7 inches
*   Passenger Volume: 98.7 cubic feet

## 2023 HR-V Interior Design & Features

The Honda HR-V cabin takes comfort a step further by offering plenty of next-level features, as well as generous seating and dimensions. You can take advantage of several of the features to help you save space and store your belongings. Here’s a closer look at some of the highlighted Honda HR-V features:

*   Air Conditioning with Air-Filtration System
*   Illuminated Steering Wheel-Mounted Controls
*   Chrome Door Pulls
*   Cargo Area Tie-Down Anchors
*   High-Deck Center Console with Sliding Armrest and Storage Compartment
*   Cargo Area Light
*   Available Automatic Climate Control
*   Available Heated Front Seats
*   Available Leather Seating

## Step Inside the Honda HR-V Interior at First Texas Honda

Article content

I’m probably the most excited about the incoming new-for-2023 Honda HR-V because of several test-drives of the first-generation model over the years.

Article content

After a few thousand kilometres of testing two separate first-gen units, I found the original HR-V to tick a lot of boxes that are important to me. Its highly canine-friendly load-in height and walk-through access can easily accommodate just about any size or age of dog. The flat rear floor makes a perfect canine lounge, and the flip-up seats mean your four-legged passengers can walk through the cabin to board and exit — no turning around required. The original HR-V was also a highly-competent winter driving machine, it handled nicely, and its flexible cabin has some special tricks that add plenty of clever versatility.

The second-generation HR-V is arriving soon; we’ll compare key dimensions and measurements to the first-generation machine, as well as to some other popular crossovers to help perspective shoppers size it up.

Article content

[**Compare these crossovers: Honda HR-V vs Toyota Corolla Cross vs Subaru Crosstrek**](https://driving.ca/comparison-results/154179-152890-151917/2022-honda-hr-v-sport-awd-vs-2022-toyota-corolla-cross-le-cvt-awd-vs-2022-subaru-crosstrek-sport-with-eyesight-cvt/)

Article content

And size it up, they have. The latest machine is longer and wider than the original, which helps to give it one of the biggest cargo capacities in its class, as well as more rear seat legroom than the first-generation unit.

Article content

The new HR-V’s 2,655 mm wheelbase stretches the distance between front and rear wheels by 45 mm, compared to the first-generation HR-V’s 2,610 mm wheelbase. On overall length, the 2023 HR-V measures in at 4,568 mm, 209 mm longer than its predecessor at 4,348 mm.The new HR-V is 1,620 mm tall, a 15 mm increase from its predecessor’s height of 1,605 mm.

Article content

Passenger volume improves accordingly for 2023, with up to 2,794 litres of interior volume in the latest HR-V versus 2,721L for the first-generation machine. That’s an improvement of 73 litres, about half the trunk-space of a Mazda MX-5.On headroom, the new HR-V measures in with 976 mm up front and 964 in the rear — improvements of 21 mm and 9 mm respectively, when comparing models with the sunroof.You’ll find 1,064 mm of front seat leg room in the 2023 HR-V, an increase of 17mm.Shoulder room is down 5 mm in the front seats, but grows by 18 mm in the rear.

Article content

Overall, the 2023 HR-V’s track width (the distance between two wheels on the same axle) is increased by about 55 mm up front and 64 mm in the rear. The body swallows it all up — its overall width clocking in at 70 mm wider than the first-generation machine for a total of 2,089 mm including the mirrors.

Article content

With AWD, the new HR-V weighs in at 1,431 kilograms — 78 kg heavier than the first-generation machine with AWD equipped. The new engine produces 158 horsepower, an increase of 17 hp, but changes to fuel economy are marginal. Despite the additional size, weight, and output, the average fuel consumption of AWD-equipped HR-V models is rated at 8.7 L/100 km for model-year 2023 — just a tick more than the 8.5 L/100 km combined rating of the first-generation unit. A ssuming an annual distance driven of 25,000 kilometres and a fuel price of $2.00 per litre, the bigger second-generation HR-V will tend to drink about $134 dollars more fuel annually than the first-gen.

Article content

A notable competitor to the 2023 Honda HR-V is the 2022 Toyota Corolla Cross — it’s smaller and more powerful, offers similar cargo volume, more headroom and front-seat legroom, and notably better fuel economy from the standard engine. A hybrid engine is on the way, too. At this writing, the HR-V only offers a standard gasoline engine, no hybrid option yet.

Article content

What about the Subaru Crosstrek? It trails the HR-V’s passenger volume by 33 litres, and gives the HR-V a 21 mm advantage in front-seat headroom, and a 4 mm advantage in rear seat headroom. The Crosstrek serves up 31 mm more front-seat legroom though, but it’s the HR-V in the lead for seats-up cargo volume, with a full 100 litre advantage here — that’s an extra camping cooler worth of space for the Honda.

Article content

Advertisement 4

Story continues below

Article content

Compared to its big brother the CR-V, the 2023 Honda HR-V is just 18 mm shorter from tip to tail, though the CR-V is the taller sibling by nearly 70 mm. This shows up in the cargo volume figures: the HR-V will hold up to 1,559 litres of your stuff, though the CR-V bumps that figure to 2,146 litres, an advantage of 587 litres, which is more than the seats-up cargo capacity of a Hyundai Kona.

Article content

To help you visualize the HR-V’s size, the two closest competitors I could find included the VW ID.4 and Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross — both of which are within a centimetre or two of the HR-V, where major dimensions are concerned. By the way, that’s about 32 mm shorter than a Toyota RAV4, and just a little taller than a Jeep Compass.

Article content

[**Compare these HR-V competitors: Honda HR-V vs Volkswagen ID.4 vs Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross**](https://driving.ca/comparison-results/154179-148050-154214/2022-honda-hr-v-sport-awd-vs-2022-mitsubishi-eclipse-cross-se-s-awc-vs-2022-volkswagen-id4-pro/)

The new HR-V is built on a Civic-based platform, and it’s new look and dimensions come alongside an underlying recipe that’s remained largely the same — specifically, by blending good fuel economy, plenty of space, and plenty of flexibility into a handy and easy-to-use package. If you’re a current HR-V fan looking for a bit of an upgrade and up-size, the new HR-V is built to do the trick.

It’s one of many fresh and compelling new choices in a rapidly growing segment. Pricing begins in the high-twenties for front-wheel drive, while AWD-equipped units come in from the low-thirties.

Justin Pritchard is an experienced motoring expert whose work is read and watched by Canadians across the country on a weekly basis. If you’re a current HR-V fan looking for a bit of an upgrade and up-size, the new HR-V is built to do the trick

Article content

I’m probably the most excited about the incoming new-for-2023 Honda HR-V because of several test-drives of the first-generation model over the years.

Article content

After a few thousand kilometres of testing two separate first-gen units, I found the original HR-V to tick a lot of boxes that are important to me. Its highly canine-friendly load-in height and walk-through access can easily accommodate just about any size or age of dog. The flat rear floor makes a perfect canine lounge, and the flip-up seats mean your four-legged passengers can walk through the cabin to board and exit — no turning around required. The original HR-V was also a highly-competent winter driving machine, it handled nicely, and its flexible cabin has some special tricks that add plenty of clever versatility.

The second-generation HR-V is arriving soon; we’ll compare key dimensions and measurements to the first-generation machine, as well as to some other popular crossovers to help perspective shoppers size it up.

Article content

[**Compare these crossovers: Honda HR-V vs Toyota Corolla Cross vs Subaru Crosstrek**](https://driving.ca/comparison-results/154179-152890-151917/2022-honda-hr-v-sport-awd-vs-2022-toyota-corolla-cross-le-cvt-awd-vs-2022-subaru-crosstrek-sport-with-eyesight-cvt/)

And size it up, they have. The latest machine is longer and wider than the original, which helps to give it one of the biggest cargo capacities in its class, as well as more rear seat legroom than the first-generation unit.

Article content

The new HR-V’s 2,655 mm wheelbase stretches the distance between front and rear wheels by 45 mm, compared to the first-generation HR-V’s 2,610 mm wheelbase. On overall length, the 2023 HR-V measures in at 4,568 mm, 209 mm longer than its predecessor at 4,348 mm.The new HR-V is 1,620 mm tall, a 15 mm increase from its predecessor’s height of 1,605 mm.

Article content

Passenger volume improves accordingly for 2023, with up to 2,794 litres of interior volume in the latest HR-V versus 2,721L for the first-generation machine. That’s an improvement of 73 litres, about half the trunk-space of a Mazda MX-5.On headroom, the new HR-V measures in with 976 mm up front and 964 in the rear — improvements of 21 mm and 9 mm respectively, when comparing models with the sunroof.You’ll find 1,064 mm of front seat leg room in the 2023 HR-V, an increase of 17mm.Shoulder room is down 5 mm in the front seats, but grows by 18 mm in the rear.

Article content

Overall, the 2023 HR-V’s track width (the distance between two wheels on the same axle) is increased by about 55 mm up front and 64 mm in the rear. The body swallows it all up — its overall width clocking in at 70 mm wider than the first-generation machine for a total of 2,089 mm including the mirrors.

Article content

With AWD, the new HR-V weighs in at 1,431 kilograms — 78 kg heavier than the first-generation machine with AWD equipped. The new engine produces 158 horsepower, an increase of 17 hp, but changes to fuel economy are marginal. Despite the additional size, weight, and output, the average fuel consumption of AWD-equipped HR-V models is rated at 8.7 L/100 km for model-year 2023 — just a tick more than the 8.5 L/100 km combined rating of the first-generation unit. A ssuming an annual distance driven of 25,000 kilometres and a fuel price of $2.00 per litre, the bigger second-generation HR-V will tend to drink about $134 dollars more fuel annually than the first-gen.

Article content

A notable competitor to the 2023 Honda HR-V is the 2022 Toyota Corolla Cross — it’s smaller and more powerful, offers similar cargo volume, more headroom and front-seat legroom, and notably better fuel economy from the standard engine. A hybrid engine is on the way, too. At this writing, the HR-V only offers a standard gasoline engine, no hybrid option yet.

Article content

What about the Subaru Crosstrek? It trails the HR-V’s passenger volume by 33 litres, and gives the HR-V a 21 mm advantage in front-seat headroom, and a 4 mm advantage in rear seat headroom. The Crosstrek serves up 31 mm more front-seat legroom though, but it’s the HR-V in the lead for seats-up cargo volume, with a full 100 litre advantage here — that’s an extra camping cooler worth of space for the Honda.

Article content

Advertisement 4

Story continues below

Article content

Compared to its big brother the CR-V, the 2023 Honda HR-V is just 18 mm shorter from tip to tail, though the CR-V is the taller sibling by nearly 70 mm. This shows up in the cargo volume figures: the HR-V will hold up to 1,559 litres of your stuff, though the CR-V bumps that figure to 2,146 litres, an advantage of 587 litres, which is more than the seats-up cargo capacity of a Hyundai Kona.

Article content

To help you visualize the HR-V’s size, the two closest competitors I could find included the VW ID.4 and Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross — both of which are within a centimetre or two of the HR-V, where major dimensions are concerned. By the way, that’s about 32 mm shorter than a Toyota RAV4, and just a little taller than a Jeep Compass.

Article content

[**Compare these HR-V competitors: Honda HR-V vs Volkswagen ID.4 vs Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross**](https://driving.ca/comparison-results/154179-148050-154214/2022-honda-hr-v-sport-awd-vs-2022-mitsubishi-eclipse-cross-se-s-awc-vs-2022-volkswagen-id4-pro/)

Article content

The new HR-V is built on a Civic-based platform, and it’s new look and dimensions come alongside an underlying recipe that’s remained largely the same — specifically, by blending good fuel economy, plenty of space, and plenty of flexibility into a handy and easy-to-use package. If you’re a current HR-V fan looking for a bit of an upgrade and up-size, the new HR-V is built to do the trick.

Article content

It’s one of many fresh and compelling new choices in a rapidly growing segment. Pricing begins in the high-twenties for front-wheel drive, while AWD-equipped units come in from the low-thirties.

## Justin Pritchard

Justin Pritchard is a Sudbury, Ontario based automotive journalist and award-winning presenter, photographer, videographer and technical writer. Every week, Justin uses his keyboard, voice and cameras to share his latest automotive reviews and discoveries with his audience, via multiple Canadian television programs, print and online publications. 
### Currently

 Technical Writer, Videographer, Presenter, Producer, Driving.ca Contributor, Host of EastLink Community TV's 'AutoPilot', Award-Winning Photographer 
### Education

 Laurentian University, B.Comm Summary · 18 years of weekly automotive reviews with over 900 published road tests · 1,000,000 kilometers of road testing and counting · Award-winning videographer, photographer, technical writer and presenter · Award-winning road safety journalist and winter driving expert. 
### EXPERIENCE

Justin Pritchard is an experienced motoring expert whose work is read and watched by Canadians across the country on a weekly basis. Starting his career at Auto123.com back in 2005 (while finishing his final year of studies at Laurentian University in Sudbury, Ontario), Justin quickly applied his passion for writing, presenting, and photography, working under some of the most recognized editors in the Canadian motoring scene.

Justin has written one of the largest collections of used car buyer guides on the internet, and his TV program, AutoPilot, has aired over 600 episodes across 16 seasons. Presently, AutoPilot is the only English-language motoring program on Canadian cable TV, though he's lent his informative style and easy-to-identify voice to video features for Youtube, Driving.ca, Autotrader.ca, Motoring TV, and elsewhere. With 4 years as co-chair of the Canadian Car of the Year Awards (CCOTY) program, a passion for vehicle testing shines though in all of his work.

A passion for photography from a young age makes Justin as comfortable behind the camera as in front of it, and capturing motoring memories from the scenery of beautiful Northern Ontario is a priority in much of his work. The particularly harsh winter climate in this part of Canada makes Justin a particular expert on winter driving, winter tires, and extreme-weather safety.

### EDUCATION

 Justin earned a Bachelor of Commerce (Hons) from Laurentian University in 2005. 
### Major awards won by the author

 2019 AJAC Video Journalism Award (Winner) 2019 AJAC Road Safety Journalism Award (Runner-Up) 2019 AJAC Automotive Writing (vehicle review topics) (Winner) 2019 AJAC Automotive Writing (technical topics) (Winner) 2018 AJAC Journalist of the Year

## **Overview**

[**Honda**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda) has given its 2023 HR-V a complete makeover, the better to combat the onslaught of desirable and stylish small SUVs that have flooded the market. The [**outgoing generation**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/hr-v) was practical and offered good value but it lagged the segment's best—the [**Hyundai Kona**](https://www.caranddriver.com/hyundai/kona), the [**Kia Seltos**](https://www.caranddriver.com/kia/seltos), and the [**Mazda CX-30**](https://www.caranddriver.com/mazda/cx-30)—in almost every way. No surprise then that the new HR-V looks totally different from the outgoing model. The new HR-V shares its platform with the Civic and uses a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter inline-four from Honda's **[compact sedan](https://www.caranddriver.com/rankings/best-sedans/compact)**. Gone, sadly, is the outgoing model's trick second-row Magic Seat, which flipped down to make the HR-V one of the most flexible cargo-friendly small SUVs. But the new generation is wider and longer, which Honda claims benefits interior space. Independent rear suspension replaces the old model's torsion beam setup, a change that promises to improve ride and handling. The new model also receives updated infotainment features and more modern driver-assistance technology.

## **Engine, Transmission, and Performance**

In Europe, the HR-V is powered by a hybrid powertrain borrowed from the [**Insight**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/insight) and [**Accord**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/accord) but the U.S. version comes with a traditional gasoline 2.0-liter four-cylinder that's good for 158 horsepower. If that sounds familiar, it's because the same engine serves as the base powertrain in the Civic. The HR-V managed a 9.4-second launch to 60 mph during our acceleration testing. That's over a full second slower than the more powerful non-turbo **[Mazda CX-30](https://www.caranddriver.com/mazda/cx-30)** and two-tenths slower than the 147-hp [**Hyundai Kona**](https://www.caranddriver.com/hyundai/kona). In the HR-V, the 2.0-liter four-cylinder feels lethargic and gutless, but since the SUV shares its platform with the Civic, we could see a 180-hp turbocharged 1.5-liter or a hybrid powertrain join the lineup down the road. For now, front-wheel drive and a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) are the standard arrangement but all-wheel drive is available as an option on all trims. The outgoing HR-V didn't deliver the quiet athleticism we expect of Hondas, but this new generation corrects that with a chassis inherited from the spry Civic.

## **Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG**

Fuel economy estimates are highest on front-wheel-drive models, which are rated at 26 mpg city and 32 mpg highway. Going with all-wheel drive drops the city rating to 25 mpg and the highway rating to 30 mpg. During our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test route the HR-V beat its EPA estimate by 2 mpg. And we managed 440 miles of highway driving on a single tank of gas. For more information about the HR-V's fuel economy, visit the [**EPA's website**](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/findacar.shtml).

## **Interior, Comfort, and Cargo**

The HR-V adopts a more modern interior design inspired by the redesigned Civic's; it's both classic and attractive. The front seats are comfortable and supportive while providing a wide range of adjustments. The outgoing model offered Honda's novel second-row Magic Seat, which allows the rear bench to flip and fold to create an especially low, flat floor. That feature helped the HR-V lead the segment in cargo capacity despite its diminutive size. Unfortunately, the new HR-V has abandoned that feature, but Honda claims that the new model's cargo bay is larger and that lift-over height has been reduced to aid with loading heavy items.

## **Infotainment and Connectivity**

All models come with either a 7.0- or 9.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto; the larger display offers wireless connectivity for those features, but it's limited to the top EX-L trim. Also standard on the EX-L is a wireless smartphone charging pad. We also expect to see features such as SiriusXM satellite radio, in-dash navigation, and a Wi-Fi hotspot, at least as options.

## **Warranty and Maintenance Coverage**

Honda's standard warranty package is fairly basic, and rival SUVs such as the Kona and Seltos come with much longer coverage plans. Buyers of the HR-V will find a two-year complimentary maintenance plan, though, and that's something that the Kia doesn't offer.

*   **Limited warranty covers 3 years or 36,000 miles**
*   **Powertrain warranty covers 5 years or 60,000 miles**
*   **Complimentary scheduled maintenance is covered for 2 years or 24,000 miles**

## **Overview**

[**Honda**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda) has given its 2023 HR-V a complete makeover, the better to combat the onslaught of desirable and stylish small SUVs that have flooded the market. The [**outgoing generation**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/hr-v) was practical and offered good value but it lagged the segment's best—the [**Hyundai Kona**](https://www.caranddriver.com/hyundai/kona), the [**Kia Seltos**](https://www.caranddriver.com/kia/seltos), and the [**Mazda CX-30**](https://www.caranddriver.com/mazda/cx-30)—in almost every way. No surprise then that the new HR-V looks totally different from the outgoing model. The new HR-V shares its platform with the Civic and uses a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter inline-four from Honda's **[compact sedan](https://www.caranddriver.com/rankings/best-sedans/compact)**. Gone, sadly, is the outgoing model's trick second-row Magic Seat, which flipped down to make the HR-V one of the most flexible cargo-friendly small SUVs. But the new generation is wider and longer, which Honda claims benefits interior space. Independent rear suspension replaces the old model's torsion beam setup, a change that promises to improve ride and handling. The new model also receives updated infotainment features and more modern driver-assistance technology.

## **Engine, Transmission, and Performance**

In Europe, the HR-V is powered by a hybrid powertrain borrowed from the [**Insight**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/insight) and [**Accord**](https://www.caranddriver.com/honda/accord) but the U.S. version comes with a traditional gasoline 2.0-liter four-cylinder that's good for 158 horsepower. If that sounds familiar, it's because the same engine serves as the base powertrain in the Civic. The HR-V managed a 9.4-second launch to 60 mph during our acceleration testing. That's over a full second slower than the more powerful non-turbo **[Mazda CX-30](https://www.caranddriver.com/mazda/cx-30)** and two-tenths slower than the 147-hp [**Hyundai Kona**](https://www.caranddriver.com/hyundai/kona). In the HR-V, the 2.0-liter four-cylinder feels lethargic and gutless, but since the SUV shares its platform with the Civic, we could see a 180-hp turbocharged 1.5-liter or a hybrid powertrain join the lineup down the road. For now, front-wheel drive and a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) are the standard arrangement but all-wheel drive is available as an option on all trims. The outgoing HR-V didn't deliver the quiet athleticism we expect of Hondas, but this new generation corrects that with a chassis inherited from the spry Civic.

## **Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG**

Fuel economy estimates are highest on front-wheel-drive models, which are rated at 26 mpg city and 32 mpg highway. Going with all-wheel drive drops the city rating to 25 mpg and the highway rating to 30 mpg. During our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test route the HR-V beat its EPA estimate by 2 mpg. And we managed 440 miles of highway driving on a single tank of gas. For more information about the HR-V's fuel economy, visit the [**EPA's website**](https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/findacar.shtml).

## **Interior, Comfort, and Cargo**

The HR-V adopts a more modern interior design inspired by the redesigned Civic's; it's both classic and attractive. The front seats are comfortable and supportive while providing a wide range of adjustments. The outgoing model offered Honda's novel second-row Magic Seat, which allows the rear bench to flip and fold to create an especially low, flat floor. That feature helped the HR-V lead the segment in cargo capacity despite its diminutive size. Unfortunately, the new HR-V has abandoned that feature, but Honda claims that the new model's cargo bay is larger and that lift-over height has been reduced to aid with loading heavy items.

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Review

[![Image 7: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   Generous standard equipment
*   Excellent safety scores
*   Well-considered interior
*   Great resale values

### Cons

*   All-wheel drive not offered
*   No hybrid version available

### What's New?

*   Sport trim joins the lineup
*   Free maintenance over two years/24,000 miles
*   Sonic Gray Pearl added to the paint choices
*   Previous LX base version discontinued

The 2023 Honda Odyssey minivan comes with a new trim for its entry level, plus a completely fresh mid-range Sport model. These are the main changes for the new model year, yet the Odyssey really didn’t have to do anything different. Because it’s already superb at what it does.

There are so many areas where the Odyssey is strong. It’s spacious, well built, well thought out, refined, and reliable. It’s been made a Top Safety Pick+ by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and awarded the maximum 5-Star score by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

The Odyssey also has its fans at Kelley Blue Book. The 2020 model took [Best Buy](https://www.kbb.com/awards/best-buy-awards-minivan-van-2020/) and Best Resale Value awards for the minivan class.

This generation launched for 2018, but has kept up to date with improvements along the way. Despite its name, the new Sport trim doesn’t add more power or swap in a firmer suspension. It brings a specific look and is otherwise equipped like the EX-L, which is $800 cheaper.

### 2023 Honda Odyssey Pricing

2023 Honda Odyssey pricing starts at $28,500 for the Odyssey EX Minivan 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $38,865 when new. The range-topping 2023 Odyssey Elite Minivan 4D starts at $33,300 today, originally priced from $50,995.

### Driving the Honda Odyssey

A minivan is never going to spark desire, but those with enough children to need a minivan presumably have their desires sparked in other ways. So buyers are no doubt happy to have something with reasonable power for getting up to speed on the freeway, decent fuel economy, a comfortable ride quality, and a general easiness to the whole experience.

That’s exactly what the 2023 Odyssey minivan supplies. There’s a serenity that fraught parents will appreciate, from the power delivery to the gearshifts. The Odyssey is the last thing anyone needs to worry about. This is especially true in light of the driver assistance features that come as standard across the range. For example, blind-spot monitoring is an absolute boon in a vehicle this size.

### Interior Comfort

Seating for eight is standard in the 2023 Odyssey minivan. And only one of them has to be a little less extravagant with their beverages, since there are 15 cupholders.

Space is plentiful in all three seating rows. And between the folding and sliding of various positions (the back row folds into the floor), there should be enough versatility for carrying people and/or cargo to please most buyers.

In common with the rest of the Honda portfolio, cabin materials are of decent quality, with excellent fit and finish. Just above the rearview mirror is a concave mirror for quick checks on the passengers behind.

Sport trim’s leather seating surfaces — on the front seats and outboard second-row positions — are black, with red stitching. This color scheme applies to the steering wheel as well. The headliner is also black.

The top two trims have the CabinWatch rear-seat monitor and CabinTalk, where the driver’s voice is piped through either the headphones of the rear-seat entertainment system (Touring trim) or both the headphones and the rear speakers (Elite trim).

### Exterior Styling

Powered sliding passenger doors on both sides are standard with every 2023 Odyssey, another considerate feature for harassed parents. And a powered tailgate comes in at the second trim level.

The new Sport trim is third, right in the middle of the range. It has a lot of exterior details finished in gloss black, like the grille, side mirror housings, B-pillars, rear pillars, light surrounds, and taillight trim.

The wheels are also finished in black. This is the first trim level where 19-inch alloy wheels are standard. This brings up an aspect to keep in mind on the test drive — we preferred the smoother ride quality of the 18-inch wheel/tire combination on the lower two trims.

Sport trim is available in Platinum White Pearl, Crystal Black Pearl, Radiant Red Metallic, and Sonic Gray Pearl. This last color also is available on the Touring and the Elite.

### Favorite Features

MAGIC SLIDE SECOND-ROW SEATS  
 These seats can move forward, reducing the distance between a parent up front and a young one in a child seat just behind. They also make it easier to access the rearmost seats, as well as being able to move back, optimizing legroom. They can even move side to side, providing extra versatility.

SMART ENTRY WITH WALK-AWAY AUTO LOCK  
 For parents, big families often mean not enough hands. This feature does away with the need to dig for keys in pockets or purses. It will unlock the Odyssey minivan on approach, and secure everything once the clan has disembarked.

### Standard Features

With EX becoming the new entry point into Honda Odyssey minivan ownership, the level of standard equipment is high. This includes 18-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights/daytime running lights/fog lights/taillights, keyless entry/ignition, smart locking, 3-zone automatic climate control (with extra controls in the second row), 12-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, heated front seats, Magic Slide second-row seats, one 12-volt outlet up front, and another 12-volt outlet in the cargo area.

There’s a well-stocked set of driver assistance features including forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking and pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, and adaptive cruise control.

The infotainment system has an 8-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto smartphone integration, satellite radio, Bluetooth, two USB ports, and seven speakers.

### Factory Options

For about $3,0000 more, we recommend the EX-L trim for its powered/height-programmable tailgate, powered moonroof, acoustic glass windshield, leather-wrapped steering wheel, leather seating surfaces for the front seats and outboard second-row seats, driver’s-seat memory settings, two more USB ports for the second row, and an extra 12-volt outlet (in the third row).

Going to a higher trim is the method for acquiring more equipment, since the actual options list features minor stuff like bike racks and splash guards.

New for 2023, Sport trim is essentially a cosmetics package, adding 19-inch alloy wheels and red ambient cabin lighting. It would have been nice if parking sensors and hands-free tailgate operation were available in the more affordable versions, but that’s not to be.

Touring trim brings front/rear parking sensors, rear-seat entertainment system, CabinTalk/CabinWatch, Wi-Fi, navigation with voice control, turn-by-turn directions, 115-volt outlet up front, and a USB port for the third row.

Elite trim comes with hands-free tailgate operation, acoustic glass for the side windows of rows one and two, heated steering wheel, heated/ventilated front seats, blue ambient cabin lighting, wireless charging, multi-zone audio, and an 11-speaker/550-watt sound system.

### Engine & Transmission

Every 2023 Odyssey minivan is propelled by a 3.5-liter V6. There are no turbochargers or anything similar.

Output is more than adequate, at 280 horsepower and 262 lb-ft of torque. This goes to the front wheels only (all-wheel drive is not an option) through a quietly efficient 10-speed automatic transmission.

Regular gasoline is fine. Cylinder deactivation contributes to fuel efficiency, where only three cylinders are used when possible. Plus an engine stop/restart function that can be turned off if desired.

The maximum tow rating for the 2023 Odyssey is 3,500 pounds.

### **Honda Sensing**

This is a set of driver assistance features that comes as standard in every new Honda minivan. It includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking and pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning/lane-keeping assistance, and adaptive cruise control with low-speed follow.

### **Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert**

Now that EX trim becomes the most affordable new Odyssey minivan, it means blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert is standard equipment. It warns drivers if there are any vehicles approaching at either side, whether on the freeway or reversing out of a parking space.

### **Rear-seat reminder**

When there are up to seven passengers on board, it’s possible someone or something could get left behind. That doesn’t happen with this rear-seat reminder function, which is yet another standard feature across the 2023 Odyssey minivan lineup.

## FAQs

#### How much is a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

Pricing for a new 2023 Odyssey minivan starts at $37,340. It’s $41,210 for the fresh Sport trim and almost $49.5K for the top Elite trim. These prices are then subject to a destination charge.

#### How long is a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

The overall length of the 2023 Odyssey minivan is 17.1 feet. This is virtually the same as every rival — long enough for generous interior space, yet still able to fit into a typical garage.

#### Does the 2023 Honda Odyssey have all-wheel drive?

All-wheel drive is not offered with the 2023 Odyssey minivan. If this is important, check out the Toyota Sienna or the Chrysler Pacifica.

#### Is the 2023 Honda Odyssey a good vehicle?

Yes, the 2023 Honda Odyssey is a good car, as reflected by its above-average Kelley Blue Book rating of 4.6 out of 5.

#### What is the MPG for a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

The 2023 Honda Odyssey is rated to return city/highway fuel economy of 19/28 mpg.

#### How much should a 2023 Honda Odyssey cost?

Used 2023 Honda Odyssey prices currently range from $28,500 for the EX Minivan 4D to $33,300 for the Elite Minivan 4D when purchasing from a dealership, depending on a range of factors like equipment, mileage, and condition.

#### What's the cheapest Honda Odyssey?

The cheapest 2023 Honda Odyssey is the EX Minivan 4D, with a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $28,500.

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Review

[![Image 7: Colin Ryan](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/64cec13d2ac836d957cbc6f56efc60acd3c7984d2779133ca2804a51c1f21244?s=48&d=mm&r=g)](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

By [Colin Ryan](https://www.kbb.com/author/colinryan/)

Updated January 30, 2025

Colin Ryan specializes in writing about new cars. He has done this for the Los Angeles Times, Variety, Kelley Blue Book, Autotrader, Popular Mechanics, Mazda and Lexus customer magazines, plus a bunch of enthusiast sites and publications. And he spent several years as a staff writer at BBC Top Gear magazine. During this zig-zag of a career trajectory, he has driven everything from budget Malaysian hatchbacks (yes, they exist) to scarily expensive Italian exotica.

### Pros

*   Generous standard equipment
*   Excellent safety scores
*   Well-considered interior
*   Great resale values

### Cons

*   All-wheel drive not offered
*   No hybrid version available

### What's New?

*   Sport trim joins the lineup
*   Free maintenance over two years/24,000 miles
*   Sonic Gray Pearl added to the paint choices
*   Previous LX base version discontinued

The 2023 Honda Odyssey minivan comes with a new trim for its entry level, plus a completely fresh mid-range Sport model. These are the main changes for the new model year, yet the Odyssey really didn’t have to do anything different. Because it’s already superb at what it does.

There are so many areas where the Odyssey is strong. It’s spacious, well built, well thought out, refined, and reliable. It’s been made a Top Safety Pick+ by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and awarded the maximum 5-Star score by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

The Odyssey also has its fans at Kelley Blue Book. The 2020 model took [Best Buy](https://www.kbb.com/awards/best-buy-awards-minivan-van-2020/) and Best Resale Value awards for the minivan class.

This generation launched for 2018, but has kept up to date with improvements along the way. Despite its name, the new Sport trim doesn’t add more power or swap in a firmer suspension. It brings a specific look and is otherwise equipped like the EX-L, which is $800 cheaper.

### 2023 Honda Odyssey Pricing

2023 Honda Odyssey pricing starts at $28,500 for the Odyssey EX Minivan 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $38,865 when new. The range-topping 2023 Odyssey Elite Minivan 4D starts at $33,300 today, originally priced from $50,995.

### Driving the Honda Odyssey

A minivan is never going to spark desire, but those with enough children to need a minivan presumably have their desires sparked in other ways. So buyers are no doubt happy to have something with reasonable power for getting up to speed on the freeway, decent fuel economy, a comfortable ride quality, and a general easiness to the whole experience.

That’s exactly what the 2023 Odyssey minivan supplies. There’s a serenity that fraught parents will appreciate, from the power delivery to the gearshifts. The Odyssey is the last thing anyone needs to worry about. This is especially true in light of the driver assistance features that come as standard across the range. For example, blind-spot monitoring is an absolute boon in a vehicle this size.

### Interior Comfort

Seating for eight is standard in the 2023 Odyssey minivan. And only one of them has to be a little less extravagant with their beverages, since there are 15 cupholders.

Space is plentiful in all three seating rows. And between the folding and sliding of various positions (the back row folds into the floor), there should be enough versatility for carrying people and/or cargo to please most buyers.

In common with the rest of the Honda portfolio, cabin materials are of decent quality, with excellent fit and finish. Just above the rearview mirror is a concave mirror for quick checks on the passengers behind.

Sport trim’s leather seating surfaces — on the front seats and outboard second-row positions — are black, with red stitching. This color scheme applies to the steering wheel as well. The headliner is also black.

The top two trims have the CabinWatch rear-seat monitor and CabinTalk, where the driver’s voice is piped through either the headphones of the rear-seat entertainment system (Touring trim) or both the headphones and the rear speakers (Elite trim).

### Exterior Styling

Powered sliding passenger doors on both sides are standard with every 2023 Odyssey, another considerate feature for harassed parents. And a powered tailgate comes in at the second trim level.

The new Sport trim is third, right in the middle of the range. It has a lot of exterior details finished in gloss black, like the grille, side mirror housings, B-pillars, rear pillars, light surrounds, and taillight trim.

The wheels are also finished in black. This is the first trim level where 19-inch alloy wheels are standard. This brings up an aspect to keep in mind on the test drive — we preferred the smoother ride quality of the 18-inch wheel/tire combination on the lower two trims.

Sport trim is available in Platinum White Pearl, Crystal Black Pearl, Radiant Red Metallic, and Sonic Gray Pearl. This last color also is available on the Touring and the Elite.

### Favorite Features

MAGIC SLIDE SECOND-ROW SEATS  
 These seats can move forward, reducing the distance between a parent up front and a young one in a child seat just behind. They also make it easier to access the rearmost seats, as well as being able to move back, optimizing legroom. They can even move side to side, providing extra versatility.

SMART ENTRY WITH WALK-AWAY AUTO LOCK  
 For parents, big families often mean not enough hands. This feature does away with the need to dig for keys in pockets or purses. It will unlock the Odyssey minivan on approach, and secure everything once the clan has disembarked.

### Standard Features

With EX becoming the new entry point into Honda Odyssey minivan ownership, the level of standard equipment is high. This includes 18-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights/daytime running lights/fog lights/taillights, keyless entry/ignition, smart locking, 3-zone automatic climate control (with extra controls in the second row), 12-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, heated front seats, Magic Slide second-row seats, one 12-volt outlet up front, and another 12-volt outlet in the cargo area.

There’s a well-stocked set of driver assistance features including forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking and pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, and adaptive cruise control.

The infotainment system has an 8-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto smartphone integration, satellite radio, Bluetooth, two USB ports, and seven speakers.

### Factory Options

For about $3,0000 more, we recommend the EX-L trim for its powered/height-programmable tailgate, powered moonroof, acoustic glass windshield, leather-wrapped steering wheel, leather seating surfaces for the front seats and outboard second-row seats, driver’s-seat memory settings, two more USB ports for the second row, and an extra 12-volt outlet (in the third row).

Going to a higher trim is the method for acquiring more equipment, since the actual options list features minor stuff like bike racks and splash guards.

New for 2023, Sport trim is essentially a cosmetics package, adding 19-inch alloy wheels and red ambient cabin lighting. It would have been nice if parking sensors and hands-free tailgate operation were available in the more affordable versions, but that’s not to be.

Touring trim brings front/rear parking sensors, rear-seat entertainment system, CabinTalk/CabinWatch, Wi-Fi, navigation with voice control, turn-by-turn directions, 115-volt outlet up front, and a USB port for the third row.

Elite trim comes with hands-free tailgate operation, acoustic glass for the side windows of rows one and two, heated steering wheel, heated/ventilated front seats, blue ambient cabin lighting, wireless charging, multi-zone audio, and an 11-speaker/550-watt sound system.

### Engine & Transmission

Every 2023 Odyssey minivan is propelled by a 3.5-liter V6. There are no turbochargers or anything similar.

Output is more than adequate, at 280 horsepower and 262 lb-ft of torque. This goes to the front wheels only (all-wheel drive is not an option) through a quietly efficient 10-speed automatic transmission.

Regular gasoline is fine. Cylinder deactivation contributes to fuel efficiency, where only three cylinders are used when possible. Plus an engine stop/restart function that can be turned off if desired.

The maximum tow rating for the 2023 Odyssey is 3,500 pounds.

## FAQs

#### How much is a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

Pricing for a new 2023 Odyssey minivan starts at $37,340. It’s $41,210 for the fresh Sport trim and almost $49.5K for the top Elite trim. These prices are then subject to a destination charge.

#### How long is a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

The overall length of the 2023 Odyssey minivan is 17.1 feet. This is virtually the same as every rival — long enough for generous interior space, yet still able to fit into a typical garage.

#### Does the 2023 Honda Odyssey have all-wheel drive?

All-wheel drive is not offered with the 2023 Odyssey minivan. If this is important, check out the Toyota Sienna or the Chrysler Pacifica.

#### Is the 2023 Honda Odyssey a good vehicle?

Yes, the 2023 Honda Odyssey is a good car, as reflected by its above-average Kelley Blue Book rating of 4.6 out of 5.

#### What is the MPG for a 2023 Honda Odyssey?

The 2023 Honda Odyssey is rated to return city/highway fuel economy of 19/28 mpg.

#### How much should a 2023 Honda Odyssey cost?

Used 2023 Honda Odyssey prices currently range from $28,500 for the EX Minivan 4D to $33,300 for the Elite Minivan 4D when purchasing from a dealership, depending on a range of factors like equipment, mileage, and condition.

#### What's the cheapest Honda Odyssey?

The cheapest 2023 Honda Odyssey is the EX Minivan 4D, with a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $28,500.

## FAQs

### Is the Honda Odyssey a 4 or 6 cylinder?

All trim levels of the 2023 Odyssey feature a 6 cylinder engine.

### Does the 2023 Honda Odyssey have a turbo?

No, the 2023 Odyssey does not have any trim packages that offer a turbo engine at this time.

### What features does a 2023 Odyssey have?

2023 Honda Odyssey features include AM/FM Radio, Bluetooth Wireless Technology, and Child Door Locks.

### How much horsepower does a 2023 Odyssey have?

All 2023 Odyssey trim variations have 280 horsepower.

### Is the Honda Odyssey underpowered?

It depends on your definition of underpowered. All 2023 Odyssey trim variations have 280 horsepower.

### Is the Honda Odyssey fuel efficient?

All trim levels of the 2023 Odyssey get 22 MPG, with 19 MPG in the city and 28 MPG on the highway.

Whatever your reason for wanting a bigger vehicle, consider the 2023 Honda Odyssey minivan for your Depere or Appleton drives. It’s one of the most respected minivans on the market right now.

Read more details regarding the 2023 [Honda Odyssey](https://www.vans-honda.com/new-vehicles/odyssey/) length to help you determine if it will fit in your Green Bay garage.

## How Long Is the Honda Odyssey From Front to Back?

Just how long is the 2023 Honda Odyssey from bumper to bumper? **The 2023 Honda Odyssey’s total length is 205.2 inches.**This family-friendly minivan has seating for up to eight people, so you and all your passengers have plenty of room during your weekend adventures and cross-country family vacations.

Keep reading to discover more about the 2023 Honda Odyssey’s exterior dimensions and interior specs.

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Exterior Dimensions

Before you invest in a new vehicle, make sure it will fit comfortably in your Manitowoc garage. Take a closer look at the 2023 Honda Odyssey’s exterior dimensions to get an idea of the measurements compared to your garage. You might have to move some stuff around, and don’t forget to leave enough room to open the two front doors of your minivan.

*   **Wheelbase:** 118.1 in
*   **Length:** 205.2 inches
*   **Height:** 69.6 inches
*   **Width:** 78.5 inches

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Interior Dimensions

Minivans are great because of the thoughtfully designed interior cabin, giving your passengers plenty of room to stretch out on long trips while having enough cargo space for weekly shopping trips and fun-filled vacations. Don’t forget about packing for weekend getaways across WI, whether you head to your favorite fishing spot or a resort destination.

Expect posh comfort and maximum relaxation thanks to the 2023 Honda Odyssey’s interior space.

*   **Headroom (Front/Middle/Rear):** 40.7 in / 39.5 in / 38.3 in
*   **Shoulder Room (Front/Middle/Rear):** 63.1 in / 61.6 in / 60.0 in
*   **Hip room (Front/Middle/Rear):** 58.6 in / 64.8 in / 48.4 in
*   **Shoulder Room (Front/Middle/Rear):** 63.1 in / 61.6 in / 60.0 in

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Cargo Space Measurements

Another benefit of owning a 2023 Honda Odyssey is the versatile cargo solutions with plenty of space for weekly grocery runs, sporting equipment for your kids’ practices and games, and luggage for family vacations. Honda makes it easy to handle any cargo you need to haul.

Look at the cargo capacity of the 2023 Honda Odyssey.

*   **Cargo Volume Behind Third Row:** 32.8 cu ft* / 38.6 cu ft
*   **Cargo Volume Behind Second Row:** 89.2 cu ft* / 92.3 cu ft
*   **Cargo Volume Behind First Row:** 144.9 cu ft* / 158.0 cu ft

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Interior Features

The 2023 Honda Odyssey’s length and dimensions can handle everything your family needs as you cruise around Green Bay and the surrounding area. Even better, the interior comes with several modern amenities and high-tech features that maximize your storage space, allow people to get comfy and cozy, and help you stay in control of your vehicle while delivering the convenience that modern drivers need.

Some of the highlights you can find on this year’s Honda Odyssey include:

*   Available Hands-Free Tailgate
*   Available Magic Slide® Second-Row Seats
*   Available Heated and Ventilated Seats
*   Wireless Phone Charging
*   10.2-Inch Rear Entertainment System
*   7-Inch Digital Driver Information Interface
*   Leather-Trimmed Interior
*   Cabinwatch® and Cabintalk® Technology for Communicating with Backseat Passengers
*   Power-Sliding Doors for Quick Access

# How Much Can You Fit in the 2023 Honda Odyssey Minivan?

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Passenger and Cargo Capacities

Minivans should have never been the butt of jokes years ago. Anyone cracking wise over a minivan being a vehicle purely for squares clearly had a blind spot as to how fantastic a minivan can actually be – and that was before today’s exciting advancements! Enter the 2023 Honda Odyssey, a vehicle that families have been relying on for years. Given its class of automobile, you may be wondering how much you can actually fit in it. Let’s take a closer look at the 2023 Honda Odyssey passenger and cargo capacities.

**[View Our Entire Inventory of New Honda Models](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/new-vehicles/)**

### ![Image 5: 2023 Honda Odyssey seats side view](https://di-uploads-pod23.dealerinspire.com/rairdonshondaofmarysville/uploads/2022/08/2023-Honda-Odyssey-seats_o.jpg)How Many People Can Sit Inside?

The 2023 Honda Odyssey is offered in five trims: EX, EX-L, Sport, Touring, and Elite. All models have a total seating capacity of eight passengers, with a total passenger volume of 163.6 cubic feet in the EX model and 160.1 cubic feet in the rest of the lineup.

Legroom can often be an issue in family vehicles, especially ones that can fit this many people, so you may be pleased to know that each row offers ample legroom. That amounts to 40.9 inches in the front and middle rows, and 38.1 inches in the rear.

### What’s the Cargo Volume?

Inside the EX variation of the 2023 Honda Odyssey, you’ll find 32.8 cubic feet of cargo space for your items. If you don’t need to use all three rows of seats, you can fold down the third row and open it up to 89.2 cubic feet of room. Finally, behind the first row, you’ll have 144.9 cubic feet to work with if you need to use all that room for bigger (or simply many more) items.*

In the rest of the lineup, those numbers read 32.8 cubic feet behind the third row, 86.6 cubic feet behind the second row, and 140.7 cubic feet behind the first row.*

We also have a [service center](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/service/) you can use after you drive off in your new vehicle, giving you peace of mind that your Honda can be well maintained. We’ll take care of you throughout the purchase or lease process and beyond.

*Based on SAE J1100 cargo volume measurement standard.

# How Much Can You Fit in the 2023 Honda Odyssey Minivan?

 August 22nd, 2022 by[Rairdon's Honda of Marysville](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/author/supportimcsweb-com/ "Posts by Rairdon's Honda of Marysville")

 Share this Post: [Share on Facebook](javascript:void(0);)[Share on Twitter](javascript:void(0);)

![Image 4: 2023 Honda Odyssey with family approaching](https://di-uploads-pod23.dealerinspire.com/rairdonshondaofmarysville/uploads/2022/08/2023-Honda-Odyssey-and-people_o.jpg)

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Passenger and Cargo Capacities

Minivans should have never been the butt of jokes years ago. Anyone cracking wise over a minivan being a vehicle purely for squares clearly had a blind spot as to how fantastic a minivan can actually be – and that was before today’s exciting advancements! Enter the 2023 Honda Odyssey, a vehicle that families have been relying on for years. Given its class of automobile, you may be wondering how much you can actually fit in it. Let’s take a closer look at the 2023 Honda Odyssey passenger and cargo capacities.

**[View Our Entire Inventory of New Honda Models](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/new-vehicles/)**

### ![Image 5: 2023 Honda Odyssey seats side view](https://di-uploads-pod23.dealerinspire.com/rairdonshondaofmarysville/uploads/2022/08/2023-Honda-Odyssey-seats_o.jpg)How Many People Can Sit Inside?

The 2023 Honda Odyssey is offered in five trims: EX, EX-L, Sport, Touring, and Elite. All models have a total seating capacity of eight passengers, with a total passenger volume of 163.6 cubic feet in the EX model and 160.1 cubic feet in the rest of the lineup.

Legroom can often be an issue in family vehicles, especially ones that can fit this many people, so you may be pleased to know that each row offers ample legroom. That amounts to 40.9 inches in the front and middle rows, and 38.1 inches in the rear.

### What’s the Cargo Volume?

Inside the EX variation of the 2023 Honda Odyssey, you’ll find 32.8 cubic feet of cargo space for your items. If you don’t need to use all three rows of seats, you can fold down the third row and open it up to 89.2 cubic feet of room. Finally, behind the first row, you’ll have 144.9 cubic feet to work with if you need to use all that room for bigger (or simply many more) items.*

In the rest of the lineup, those numbers read 32.8 cubic feet behind the third row, 86.6 cubic feet behind the second row, and 140.7 cubic feet behind the first row.*

### Find the Odyssey in Marysville, WA

If you’re looking for a vehicle fit for the whole family, visit [Rairdon’s Honda of Marysville](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/) and browse our inventory of [new Honda Odyssey models](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/new-vehicles/odyssey/). We also have a [service center](https://www.hondaofmarysville.com/service/) you can use after you drive off in your new vehicle, giving you peace of mind that your Honda can be well maintained. We’ll take care of you throughout the purchase or lease process and beyond.

*Based on SAE J1100 cargo volume measurement standard.

Eric Brandt is a Managing Editor, with more than a decade of experience in automotive journalism. In addition to Kelley Blue Book and Autotrader, his work has appeared in The Drive, Cars & Bids, The Motley Fool, and others. Eric specializes in family vehicles guiding readers and viewers toward car choices that suit their needs, wants, and budgets. Eric lives in Wisconsin with his wife and six children, and spends his free time riding his Gold Wing, autocrossing his Corvette, and camping with his family.

### Pros

*   Family-first interior
*   Generous standard features
*   Excellent resale value

### Cons

*   No hybrid option
*   No AWD option

### What's New?

*   Nothing

**The Honda Odyssey is one of our favorite family vehicles for its infinitely useful interior, trusty powertrain, and user-friendly tech. Pricing starts at $44,245.**

The Honda Odyssey has been a trusted name in minivans for over 30 years for good reasons. It’s long served as one of our favorites in a competitive class of minivans for getting just about everything right. Its interior is spacious for both passengers and cargo, and it has some unique features that give it the most easily accessible third row of anything we’ve driven. On the tech front, it has the safety tech you need, like Honda Sensing, and the infotainment tech you want, like wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. Top it all off with a trusted powertrain, excellent resale value, and stellar safety ratings, and you have a near-perfect family hauler in the venerable Honda Odyssey.

_We’ve spent hundreds of hours driving and evaluating this generation of [minivans](https://www.kbb.com/van-minivan/best-minivans/), including the Honda Odyssey._

### What's New for 2026

Following the second mid-cycle refresh of its fifth generation last year, the Honda Odyssey continues into 2026 with no notable changes.

### 2026 Honda Odyssey Pricing

The 2026 Honda Odyssey has a starting sticker price of $44,245, with the range-topping Odyssey Elite kicking off at $53,145. But Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Pricing currently suggests paying $1,445 to $2,545 less than MSRP, depending on trim and equipment. These prices are updated weekly.

### 2026 Honda Odyssey Pricing

The Honda Odyssey has an above-average starting price for a minivan. That’s because [Honda](https://www.kbb.com/honda/) eliminated its base EX trim last year, leaving the well-equipped EX-L as its new entry-level model. When compared to a competing minivan with similar features, the Odyssey’s pricing is about average.

Before buying an Odyssey, check the Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price to know what you should really pay. Although the [Toyota Sienna](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/sienna/) is the king of minivan resale value, the Honda Odyssey comes in a close second, holding its value better than the [Kia Carnival](https://www.kbb.com/kia/carnival/) and [Chrysler Pacifica](https://www.kbb.com/chrysler/pacifica/). ## FAQs

#### How much is the 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey starts at $44,245.

#### Does the 2026 Honda Odyssey have AWD?

No, the Honda Odyssey comes exclusively with front-wheel drive (FWD). All-wheel drive (AWD) is not available on the Odyssey.

#### How many seats are in the 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is a minivan with seating for up to eight people.

#### Is the 2026 Honda Odyssey a good buy?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is a good buy for most Minivan shoppers. It gets strong ratings from our experts and most buyers are paying less than sticker price.

#### What is the MPG for a 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is rated to return city/highway fuel economy of 19/28 mpg.

#### How much should a 2026 Honda Odyssey cost?

A 2026 Honda Odyssey should cost between $42,300 and $50,600 according to Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Pricing.

#### What's the cheapest Honda Odyssey?

The cheapest 2026 Honda Odyssey is the EX-L, with a starting sticker price of $44,245 and a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $42,300.

### Pros

*   Family-first interior
*   Generous standard features
*   Excellent resale value

### Cons

*   No hybrid option
*   No AWD option

### What's New?

*   Nothing

**The Honda Odyssey is one of our favorite family vehicles for its infinitely useful interior, trusty powertrain, and user-friendly tech. Pricing starts at $44,245.**

The Honda Odyssey has been a trusted name in minivans for over 30 years for good reasons. It’s long served as one of our favorites in a competitive class of minivans for getting just about everything right. Its interior is spacious for both passengers and cargo, and it has some unique features that give it the most easily accessible third row of anything we’ve driven. On the tech front, it has the safety tech you need, like Honda Sensing, and the infotainment tech you want, like wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. Top it all off with a trusted powertrain, excellent resale value, and stellar safety ratings, and you have a near-perfect family hauler in the venerable Honda Odyssey.

_We’ve spent hundreds of hours driving and evaluating this generation of [minivans](https://www.kbb.com/van-minivan/best-minivans/), including the Honda Odyssey._

### What's New for 2026

Following the second mid-cycle refresh of its fifth generation last year, the Honda Odyssey continues into 2026 with no notable changes.

### 2026 Honda Odyssey Pricing

The 2026 Honda Odyssey has a starting sticker price of $44,245, with the range-topping Odyssey Elite kicking off at $53,145. But Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Pricing currently suggests paying $1,445 to $2,545 less than MSRP, depending on trim and equipment. These prices are updated weekly.

### 2026 Honda Odyssey Pricing

The Honda Odyssey has an above-average starting price for a minivan. That’s because [Honda](https://www.kbb.com/honda/) eliminated its base EX trim last year, leaving the well-equipped EX-L as its new entry-level model. When compared to a competing minivan with similar features, the Odyssey’s pricing is about average.

Before buying an Odyssey, check the Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price to know what you should really pay. Although the [Toyota Sienna](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/sienna/) is the king of minivan resale value, the Honda Odyssey comes in a close second, holding its value better than the [Kia Carnival](https://www.kbb.com/kia/carnival/) and [Chrysler Pacifica](https://www.kbb.com/chrysler/pacifica/). Recouping more money when selling a vehicle can mean a bigger down payment and lower monthly payments on the next one.

## FAQs

#### How much is the 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey starts at $44,245.

#### Does the 2026 Honda Odyssey have AWD?

No, the Honda Odyssey comes exclusively with front-wheel drive (FWD). All-wheel drive (AWD) is not available on the Odyssey.

#### How many seats are in the 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is a minivan with seating for up to eight people.

#### Is the 2026 Honda Odyssey a good buy?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is a good buy for most Minivan shoppers. It gets strong ratings from our experts and most buyers are paying less than sticker price.

#### What is the MPG for a 2026 Honda Odyssey?

The 2026 Honda Odyssey is rated to return city/highway fuel economy of 19/28 mpg.

#### How much should a 2026 Honda Odyssey cost?

A 2026 Honda Odyssey should cost between $42,300 and $50,600 according to Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Pricing.

#### What's the cheapest Honda Odyssey?

The cheapest 2026 Honda Odyssey is the EX-L, with a starting sticker price of $44,245 and a Kelley Blue Book Fair Purchase Price of $42,300.

## 2023 Honda Odyssey Features

If you're someone who's after a reliable minivan with lots of standard amenities, safety features, and an efficient powertrain, then the 2023 Honda Odyssey is likely the vehicle for you. It has a 3.5-liter V6 making 280 horsepower, standard 18-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights, heated front seats, and much more. For 2023, Honda has introduced a new mid-range Sport model to the lineup.

It brings unique 19-inch wheels, gloss black exterior accents, black leather upholstery with red stitching, as well as red ambient interior lighting. Meanwhile, Honda has discontinued the previous LX base model, leaving the EX as the new entry-level trim. Also, every 2023 Honda Odyssey now comes with free maintenance for over two years or 24,000 miles. The 2023 Honda Odyssey is offered in five trims: EX, EX-L, Sport, Touring, and Elite.

Keep reading to discover more about this family-friendly minivan, then take a test drive at Westshore Honda in Tampa, FL, to determine if this vehicle is right for you.

## Comfortable & Relaxing Driving Dynamics

Every 2023 Honda Odyssey features a 3.5-liter V6 that generates 280 horsepower and 262 lb-ft of torque. This engine is paired with a reliably efficient 10-speed automatic transmission that only sends power to the front wheels, as all-wheel drive is unavailable. EPA-estimated fuel economy rating for the 2023 Odyssey is 19 mpg in the city and 28 mpg on the highway.

This minivan is rated to tow up to 3,500 pounds.

![Image 8: 2023 Honda Odyssey Specs & Features slider1](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cka-dash/210-1022-WHO1166/slider1.jpg)

![Image 9: 2023 Honda Odyssey Specs & Features slider2](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cka-dash/210-1022-WHO1166/slider2.jpg)

![Image 10: 2023 Honda Odyssey Specs & Features slider3](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cka-dash/210-1022-WHO1166/slider3.jpg)

![Image 11: 2023 Honda Odyssey Specs & Features slider4](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cka-dash/210-1022-WHO1166/slider4.jpg)

## Well-Appointed Cabin

Inside, the 2023 Honda Odyssey is richly-appointed, offering almost everything modern families need. The base EX trim has cloth upholstery, heated and power-adjustable front seats, power-sliding rear doors, Honda's Magic Slide second-row seats, tri-zone automatic climate control, and second-row sunshades. The EX-L elevates the experience to luxury with standard leather upholstery, driver's seat memory settings, a moonroof, a leather-wrapped steering wheel, and a power liftgate.

Those who want to stand out can opt for the mid-range Sport trim, which distinguishes itself with red interior LED lighting and black leather upholstery with red stitching. The Touring model enhances the experience with even more tech. If you're after even more luxury features, the top-level Elite might be just what you need. It adds standard heated and ventilated front seats, a heated steering wheel, sound-reducing side and rear window glass, and a hands-free tailgate.

In terms of cargo space, the 2023 Odyssey is just as impressive. It has 32.8 to 38.6 cubic feet of cargo volume with all seats upright, 86.6 and 92.3 cubes with the rearmost seats folded down, and between 140.7 and 158 cubic feet with the third and second rows folded. These figures vary based on the model you choose.

Outside, the 2023 Odyssey features LED headlights, 18-inch alloy wheels, heated mirrors, available 19-inch wheels, automatic wipers, power-folding and auto-dimming side mirrors, etc.

## Intuitive Infotainment System

The 2023 Honda Odyssey comes standard with a straightforward 8-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay® and Android Auto™ capability, two USB ports, satellite radio, HD Radio, Bluetooth, and a seven-speaker audio system. Upper trims offer a Wi-Fi hotspot, a rear-seat entertainment system, wireless device charging, navigation, an 11-speaker premium audio system, and additional USB ports.
